E·05 Mentor contracts · the rule you signed for surfaces in-click, three days later
The rule you agreed to on Tuesday stands beside the order on Friday — with the mentor’s signature
in-click reminder · mentor signature visible · the agreement survives the call ending
The break

Tuesday the mentor said: “no NAS in Asia.” The student nodded. Friday at 03:11, NAS in Asia. The rule was in a Discord pin nobody read. The agreement died with the call.

The moment
Tuesday 14:11 · on the call · rule signed · · · · · Friday 03:11 · the rule does the work

On Tuesday at 14:11, mid-call, Luca says it: “no NAS during Asia for thirty days.” Aria nods, taps Accept, signs. The contract files itself in the ledger with the call moment, the chart state, the six-second clip of Luca’s voice, and her own counter-signature attached. Three days pass. Then it is Friday at 03:11 UTC, half awake, jet-lagged, and she opens a NAS ticket in Asia. The cockpit pauses for three seconds. The rule appears beside the order ticket — with Luca’s signature, the date she signed, and the six-second clip of his Tuesday voice already cued. She does not place the trade. The rule did the Friday work. Not Aria, not in a Discord pin nobody read, not from memory three days old. The agreement survived the call ending.

  1. Contract grammar

    captures mentor rules as structured contracts (e.g., “no NAS during Asia for student X for 30 days”). requires the student’s explicit accept.

  2. Signature

    signs the contract by both parties, with the call moment attached. archives in the ledger, immutable.

  3. In-click surface

    renders the relevant contract in the cockpit at the moment of a triggering click. shows the rule, the mentor’s signature, and the “why” clip.

  4. Soft enforcement

    flows through the consensus gate (B·03). holds three seconds with a single line: “Luca’s rule: no NAS in Asia, signed 2026-04-08.”

  5. Hard enforcement

    locks the ticket at the contracted level (e.g., size cap, instrument lock) until a typed override of 32+ characters. writes the override into the contract record.

  6. Expiry

    expires at the contracted date. renews with explicit re-signature, never silently.

  7. Outcome attribution

    shows the mentor and student on Sunday how the rule performed. recommends tightening, relaxing, or retiring it on evidence.

What is being repaired

An agreement that dies with the call is not really an agreement — it is a feeling that lasts as long as the speaker holds the room. The trader knows this, sub-consciously, and quietly trusts mentor agreements less every time one fails. After enough failed Tuesday-to-Friday gaps, the trader stops making the agreements at all. He nods politely on the call and trades the way he was going to trade anyway. The teaching is theatre.

Structured, signed, in-the-click contracts repair the distrust at its root. The Tuesday agreement is no longer a feeling that decays over seventy hours; it is an object. It survives the call ending. It surfaces beside the order at the exact moment it is being broken, with the mentor’s signature and voice attached. Hard overrides cost a thirty-two-character typed acknowledgement, written into the contract record — not silent. The mentor stops bluffing. The student stops nodding. The room earns its name back.

Before / after

  • Where the rule livespinned message→in-the-click contract
  • When the student sees the ruleSunday review→at the click, Friday 03:11
  • Override costsilent ignore→32-char typed ack, logged

One feature, one chain, one outcome: mentorship leaves the channel and stands beside the order. The Tuesday agreement does the Friday work, with the signature visible at the moment it matters.

E·06 Copilot · one voice grounded in your ledger · refuses generic wisdom
One voice that knows you — not five strangers each pretending to
single answer · cited why-chips · refusal when your own rule already answers
The break

The trader asks ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Grok, and Perplexity the same question. Each answers as if he were a stranger. None remember the last question. By minute 38 he has five votes and no edge.

The moment
Tuesday 13:21 UTC · Marco, EUR/USD short open through CPI · four LLM tabs in seven minutes · the fifth window opens

He has asked four versions of “should I hold EUR through CPI?” across ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, and Perplexity in the last seven minutes. Each answered as if he were a stranger. Each gave him a balanced three-paragraph response. He read the third paragraph of two of them as permission. The fifth window is open and he is about to paste the same prompt. Copilot intercepts. One sentence, in the product’s own voice: “you have asked four versions of this in seven minutes; the answer hasn’t changed; your own rule seven says no holds through red folder.” Beside the sentence, four cited why-chips — each one a clickable link to his own rule, his own ledger, his own contract with Luca, and the body reading from his wearable that says his heart rate has been at 96 bpm for the last eleven minutes. He closes the four tabs.

  1. Single-voice

    routes every question through Copilot, not five LLMs. refuses to be a chat with a stranger; it is a chat with the trader’s own ledger spoken back to him.

  2. Grounding

    cites the trader’s rules, ledger, mentor contracts, today-R, body state, calendar. refuses to answer from training data when the ledger has the answer.

  3. Why-chips

    renders four cited why-chips on every answer. opens the underlying record on click: the trade, the rule, the contract, the body reading.

  4. Refusal clause

    refuses to answer questions the trader’s own rule already answers. says: “your plan says no news trading; this is news trading.”

  5. Permission-seek detector

    detects when the trader is shopping for “yes” from a model. names it: “you have asked four versions of this in seven minutes; the answer hasn’t changed.”

  6. Memory

    remembers the last question across sessions, devices, weeks. refuses to start fresh as a stranger every time.

  7. Mentor handoff

    routes questions outside its grounding to the mentor agent (A·02) or a queued mentor reply — never to a hallucination.

What is being repaired

Four-LLM permission-shopping is not stupidity, and it is not a model-quality problem. It is the modern form of what traders used to do with mentors at midnight — asking four people the same question until one of them said yes. It is a fear-management ritual. The trader knows, somewhere, that he is shopping. He keeps doing it because the alternative — sitting with the fear — is harder. Better LLMs do not cure this; they accelerate it. The faster the model, the faster the ritual cycles.

The cure is a voice that refuses the ritual by name. Not a smarter model, but a grounded one — one that points the trader back to his own ledger, his own rule, his own contract, his own body. Permission-seeking, named on the third repeat, stops being a secret. The trader catches himself in the act of bargaining for confidence from confident strangers. One voice answers, because it is the only voice that knows him. The four LLM tabs are not blocked; they are simply no longer needed.

Before / after

  • Voices answering one question5 strangers→1 grounded voice
  • Permission-shopping caughtnever→on the 3rd repeat
  • Source of the answertraining data→your rule, your ledger

One feature, one chain, one outcome: the four-LLM loop ends. One voice answers, because it is the only voice that knows the trader. Permission-seeking is named when it shows up. The trader stops shopping for confident strangers.

Band F · Dashboard AI F06
Ledger, review & governance — the memory layer

Six breaks where the trader’s history scatters across broker statements, Sheets, screenshots, and three apps that don’t talk. Dashboard AI is the ledger — cryptographically signed at the moment of the trade, never on Sunday, never from memory.

F·01 Append-only ledger · signed at the moment of the trade · not Sunday from memory
The journal writes itself — you read the week, you do not reconstruct it
six beats per trade · cryptographically signed · export-able, immutable, regulator-readable
The break

Sunday: 3–5 hours reconciling broker statements, pasting Sheets, re-writing journal entries from memory, watching the recap, updating the plan nobody will enforce. The trader is a part-time bookkeeper paying $186/month for the privilege.

The moment
Sunday 19:48 UTC · Marco at the desk · last week 41 trades · the journal already exists

Sunday at 19:48. He sits down with coffee. He used to dread this hour — three to five hours reconciling MT5 statements with Sheets, copying screenshots into Notion, writing entries from a memory that is already three days old, watching himself rewrite Wednesday into the version of Wednesday he wishes had happened. Tonight the journal is already open, and he is not writing it. He is reading it. Forty-one trades, each one signed at the moment it happened. Beat one: prep, rule seven loaded, body at 62 bpm. Beat two: entry, NAS short at 14:11, Forecast EV pulled from 31 priors. Beat three: management, rule held. Beat four: exit, +1.4R, signature stamped. He scrolls. He highlights three moments worth a re-watch. He closes the laptop at 20:11. The hour he used to lose to bookkeeping is back, every Sunday, forever.

  1. Beat capture

    writes six beats per trade automatically: prep, entry, management, exit, post, review. signs each with timestamp, account, instrument, rule, body state, Forecast verdict.

  2. Append-only

    refuses edits. permits annotations as new entries layered on top. The ledger is the history, not a draft.

  3. Signature

    cryptographically signs every entry with a key the trader holds. verifies chain integrity on every Sunday review.

  4. Export

    exports CSV, JSON, PDF, broker-statement-compatible, prop-firm-compatible, accountant-compatible. preserves signature on export.

  5. Sunday view

    opens Sunday review to the stamped events, every beat already there. narrates the week as a sequence of facts, not a memory test.

  6. Search

    accepts plain-English: “losses larger than 1R on NAS in Asia in March.” returns the trades with chart, ticket, body state, rule.

  7. Audit

    stands as a regulator-readable record of what the trader did, when, why, with which rule, signed. refuses to be tampered with by Archio itself.

What is being repaired

For a decade Sunday has been a small grief tax. The trader spends three to five hours doing the work of remembering what he already lived — knowing, somewhere, that the version he writes is already a flattering reconstruction of the version that traded. Worse: the act of writing the journal becomes a substitute for practice. Hours go to bookkeeping. The body learns that “Sunday means receipts,” not “Sunday means rehearsal.” Over months the trader stops associating Sunday with growth at all.

A signed-at-the-click ledger inverts the relationship in one motion. The reconstruction is no longer the trader’s job — it was never his job technically, and now it isn’t his job culturally either. Sunday becomes reading. The body relearns that Sunday is for review, not for accounting. The trader stops paying $186 per month to be a part-time bookkeeper, and the hours come back — every week, forever.

Before / after

  • Time on Sunday review3–5 hours→11 minutes reading
  • Source of the journalmemory + screenshots→signed at the click
  • Bookkeeping cost$186 / mo→$0

One feature, one chain, one outcome: the trader does not write Sunday. He reads Sunday. The 3–5 hour reconciliation tax goes to zero. The space rented by being a bookkeeper is given back, every week, forever.

F·02 Sunday narrator · the week tells itself in plain English · from the ledger, not from memory
A Sunday recap that doesn’t lie because it can’t — the events sign their own attendance
narrated week · gap-flagged · mentor-tagged · opens to the moments worth re-watching
The break

Sunday review is a creative writing exercise. The trader remembers the 11:42 stop as a CPI hunt, not a revenge click. The journal ends up flattering the version of him who is writing it — not the one who placed the trade.

The moment
Sunday 20:14 UTC · last week’s narrative side-by-side with the ledger · three gap-flags surface

Last Sunday Marco wrote, in his own journal: “11:42 was a clean CPI hunt. I held conviction. The market shook me out and reversed.” Tonight that paragraph appears on the left side of the screen. On the right side, the ledger shows the same 11:42 entry, signed at the moment: no CPI scheduled in the window. Last trade −2R, eighteen minutes prior. Body at 96 bpm. Rule three: no re-entries within 30 min of a −2R. Status: violated. A quiet amber underline draws across the words “CPI hunt” in his own paragraph — the gap-flag, naming the lie without scolding it. The narrator, reading the ledger, has written this week’s version: “11:42 was a revenge click eighteen minutes after a −2R, on a body still elevated from the prior loss. Rule three was broken.” No flattery. Just the line of cause. He sits with it. He keeps rule three. He retires “trade my conviction.” The journal stops being a creative-writing exercise.

  1. Narrator

    reads the ledger and writes the week in plain English: where the rules held, where they bent, where they broke. refuses to flatter; cites every claim.

  2. Gap flag

    flags the moments where the trader’s narrative on Sunday last week disagreed with the ledger. shows both side by side.

  3. Mentor tag

    tags the moments that touched mentor contracts (E·05). links the mentor’s clip and the contract for re-review.

  4. Re-watch list

    compiles the 3–5 moments worth replaying with chart, ticket, body, transcript, mentor commentary. refuses to dump 80 trades on the trader.

  5. Plan teach-back

    asks 3 yes/no questions about the rules: “keep,” “tighten,” “retire”. writes the answers into the plan editor for next week.

  6. Body recap

    renders a one-line summary of recovery, tilt, sleep across the week. maps them to the trader’s P&L distribution.

  7. Co-watch

    permits sharing a re-watch list with the mentor in one tap, in the same pane. preserves privacy on items the trader chooses not to share.

What is being repaired

Self-flattering memory is not a moral failing — it is the ordinary defence the brain runs to keep self-image stable. Every Sunday the story softens. Every Sunday the trader is a slightly better version of himself than the one who clicked. Over months the journal becomes fiction with timestamps, and the man Sunday is teaching is no longer the man who shows up Tuesday. The teaching loop opens and never closes; the trader is correcting a person who does not exist.

A narrator-from-the-ledger ends the fiction without scolding. It places the two paragraphs side by side — what was written, what actually happened — and lets the trader read the gap. The flattery is named, not punished. Over four weeks the brain learns it cannot get away with the soft version anymore, and it stops writing it. The flattering version of the trader does not get the last word, because the ledger gets there first.

Before / after

  • Source of narrativememory→ledger, cited
  • Self-flattery surfaceinvisible→gap-flag underline
  • Trades to re-watch80 (overwhelming)→3–5 (worth it)

One feature, one chain, one outcome: Sunday becomes reading instead of writing. The story of the week is grounded in the ledger, not in mood. The flattering version of the trader does not get the last word.

F·03 Prop-firm exporter · statement, audit, KYC bundle · one click
The funded-account application that doesn’t take a weekend — the bundle is already on the ledger
one click · broker statements, signed ledger, audit, KYC · submitted format-correct
The break

Applying to a prop firm or an investor takes a weekend: pull statements from MT5, paste into Sheets, redact, screenshot, write a narrative, attach a KYC. Half the rejections are formatting. The other half are mistrust the trader can’t answer.

The moment
Saturday 11:02 UTC · Aria applies to Apex $50k Eval · 14-day live link generated · 8 seconds end to end

Aria opens the funded-account portal. Apex. $50k Evaluation. Last time she did this — at TopStep, four months ago — it was a weekend: pull MT5 history, paste to Sheets, redact account numbers in Photoshop, write a one-page narrative, attach a copy of her passport, format-fail at submission, fix the comma in the date column, resubmit, wait a week, get a polite rejection because the curve was “unverifiable.” This time she clicks “Compose bundle for Apex.” The system reads the format preset, builds a signed ledger CSV, attaches the rule-adherence scorecard, attaches her KYC pack, redacts her PnL absolutes per her saved mask, and renders a read-only live link valid for 14 days. Eight seconds. Apex’s reviewer opens the link Monday morning and verifies the curve against the live ledger as she trades — no screenshot to question, no statement to reconcile, no email exchange about the half-closed XAUUSD on March 11. She passes evaluation in nine days instead of writing a weekend.

  1. Bundle composer

    composes a one-click bundle: signed ledger CSV, broker-statement reconciliation, audited KPI sheet, KYC pack, plan archive, rule-adherence scorecard.

  2. Format presets

    renders per prop firm (FTMO, MFF, Apex, Topstep, etc.) or per investor. refuses to ship in a format that fails their parser.

  3. Live link

    permits a read-only live link the prop firm or investor can verify against the ledger in real-time. expires on the trader’s schedule.

  4. Privacy redaction

    redacts on the trader’s mask: PII, PnL absolute amounts, broker account numbers. preserves what the recipient needs.

  5. Mentor reference

    permits attaching a verified mentor’s reference card (A·01) with one tap. preserves the chain of trust.

  6. Resubmit

    updates the live link automatically if the trader’s ledger continues. removes the “send a fresh statement next week” cycle.

  7. Reject memory

    captures rejection reasons. recommends the next-best-fit firm or investor based on actual fit (style, drawdown, instrument).

What is being repaired

Funded-account applications are humiliations dressed as paperwork. The trader is asked, every time, to prove with screenshots that she is who she says she is — and the screenshots are forgeable, so the asker assumes the worst, and the asking becomes ritual mistrust. The trader internalises it after a few cycles: “I will be doubted forever, no matter what I produce.” She starts pre-apologising in cover letters. She stops applying to firms she could pass. The doubt is inherited from the medium, not from her record.

A signed, live, revocable bundle ends the ritual. The reviewer can verify in real time; the trader becomes a verifiable claim, not a ten-page Photoshop case. Format-rejection drops to zero because the format is the platform’s. Mistrust drops because the underlying ledger is what the reviewer reads, not the trader’s narration of it. The dignity returned is invisible until you feel it — and once felt, the trader stops carrying the weight of being doubted as a baseline.

Before / after

  • Time to applya weekend→8 seconds
  • Format-rejection rate~50%→0%
  • Reviewer trustsscreenshots→live ledger, signed

One feature, one chain, one outcome: the funded-account application stops being a weekend. The bundle is the ledger, formatted, signed, and live. The trader is back to trading on Monday morning — not redacting on Sunday night.

F·04 Tax pack · jurisdiction-aware · signed for the accountant
The tax mountain doesn’t exist — the year is already on the ledger
jurisdiction picker · CGT / FIFO / specific-id · signed CSV the accountant can paste
The break

April. The trader spends 8–14 hours pulling broker exports, reconciling FX rates, mapping FIFO, listing wash-sale candidates, and arguing with the accountant about how to value a half-closed position. The tax bill is the last word the year gets.

The moment
April 14 · 23:11 · the accountant’s email arrives · the pack is already on the ledger

April 14, 23:11 UTC. The accountant’s email arrives in his inbox: “need your year for filing, deadline is the 18th, sorry for the late notice.” Last year this email started a 14-hour scramble — broker exports for three accounts, FX rates day by day from oanda, FIFO mapping in Sheets, two long calls with the accountant about a half-closed XAUUSD position on March 11 that took three exchanges to resolve. Tonight Marco opens the platform. Tax pack · 2026 · United Kingdom · CGT · FIFO. One click. The system has been computing this all year, line by line: every fill in GBP at fill-date FX, FIFO chain pre-built, four wash-sale candidates flagged with citations, the half-closed XAUUSD already resolved at the moment of the partial. Signed CSV out. One-page narrative for the accountant. Audit trail linking every line to the underlying signed ledger entry. He attaches it to the reply at 23:14. He goes to bed at 23:16. April keeps the weekend.

  1. Jurisdiction picker

    asks once: country, region, tax year, accounting method (FIFO / specific-id / mark-to-market). persists across years.

  2. FX engine

    reads the daily reference FX rate for the trader’s base currency. computes realised P&L per trade in the local currency at fill date.

  3. Method engine

    computes CGT, FIFO, specific-id, or mark-to-market according to the picker. shows per-method totals so the accountant can argue with one set of numbers.

  4. Wash-sale detector

    flags wash-sale candidates per jurisdiction. refuses to apply rules that don’t apply (US-specific to non-US, etc.).

  5. Tax-pack export

    renders a signed CSV the accountant can paste into the local filing software. renders a one-page narrative for the trader to review.

  6. Audit trail

    links every line in the tax pack to the underlying signed ledger entry. survives a tax-authority audit because every claim has a citation.

  7. Year-over-year

    persists tax packs across years. shows trend lines for losses carried, allowances, deductions.

What is being repaired

The tax pack at year-end is the year’s last word. After eleven months of effort — the early mornings, the discipline, the signed contracts with mentors, the Sundays of review — the trader sits down to spend a 14-hour weekend reducing his entire trading life to a tax authority’s spreadsheet. The act of doing it is the single most demoralising day of his trading calendar. It is the moment he most often quits, because the year ends with him feeling like a part-time bookkeeper and not a trader.

A pre-computed, signed, jurisdiction-aware tax pack ends the demoralisation tax. The year’s last word is no longer a Sunday spent feeling like an accountant’s assistant; it is fourteen seconds in April. The trader keeps the body that traded all year, instead of trading it for the body that filed. The audit trail means an audit is no longer a panic event — every claim has a citation back to a signed ledger entry, ready before the question is asked.

Before / after

  • Time in April8–14 hours→1 click
  • FX reconciliationmanual oanda paste→fill-date, automatic
  • Argument with accountant3 calls→1 CSV with citations

One feature, one chain, one outcome: the 8–14 hour tax mountain is already on the ledger when April arrives. The accountant pastes one CSV. The trader keeps the weekend.

F·05 Verified social profile · the curve, the rules, the receipts · portable
A finance profile finance can read — one URL, one card, one verifiable answer
portable profile · audit-anchored · no Photoshop · revocable
The break

Today the trader proves himself with screenshots a child could fake. There is no portable, signed, revocable, finance-readable identity for a retail trader. He stays a stranger, forever, to every counterparty in his life.

The moment
Tuesday 14:48 UTC · recruiter call from a buy-side desk · one URL pasted in the chat · verified live

A buy-side recruiter calls Marco about a junior PM seat. The first question, every time: “send me proof of your record.” Last time he sent screenshots; she replied with a polite “we’ll be in touch” that meant no. Tonight he pastes one URL in the chat. She clicks. A profile loads: 4-year audited curve, rule-adherence per quarter, mentor associations (two, both bonded), dispute history (one, resolved in his favour), zero PII, zero account numbers, every claim clickable to a signed ledger entry verified live against the platform. She verifies one specific line — the curve in May 2025 — by clicking it; the system shows her the underlying 14 trades that built it, in real time, signed. She closes the call by asking when he can fly out. Two days later he revokes the URL with one click; the profile is gone, the verification record is preserved on the platform’s side. The screenshot economy ended for him on Tuesday at 14:48.

  1. Profile composer

    composes a public profile from the trader’s ledger: tenure, audited curve, rule-adherence, mentor associations, dispute history. refuses to render unverified claims.

  2. Granular toggles

    permits the trader to publish only what he chooses: curve shape without absolutes, instruments without sizes, rules without account ids.

  3. URL + card

    renders one URL and one card. shareable on X, in DMs, in pitch decks, in funded-account applications.

  4. Counterparty verify

    permits a recruiter, a prop firm, a regulator, or a journalist to verify the card’s claims against the ledger live. refuses to allow the card to lie.

  5. Revocation

    revokes the URL on one click. preserves the trader’s sovereignty over his own record.

  6. Mentor reference

    permits the trader to attach a mentor’s reference card (A·01). preserves the chain of trust on the social side.

  7. Audit trail

    renders for the verifier the timestamp of each underlying ledger entry. survives the profile being shared off-platform.

What is being repaired

For two decades retail traders have lived in a screenshot economy where every claim is forgeable and therefore every claimant is doubted. The cost is not visible because the trader does not know what it would feel like to not be doubted. He pre-apologises in cover letters. He under-states his record because he expects scepticism. He stops asking for things he could ask for — recruiter calls, allocations, sponsorships — because the proof he can produce will not survive the asking.

A portable, signed, revocable profile lets him feel the absence of doubt for the first time. The recruiter believes him — not because she trusts him, but because she trusts the platform underneath, and that trust is not a slogan, it is a click that returns a ledger entry. Once felt, the absence of doubt becomes obvious in retrospect: the trader was carrying the weight of being-doubted-as-a-baseline the whole time. With sovereignty preserved — one-click revoke, granular publish toggles — he is finally verifiable on his own terms.

Before / after

  • Proof of recordscreenshot→audited URL
  • Falsifiabilitynone→verified live against ledger
  • Sovereigntypermanent claim→one-click revoke

One feature, one chain, one outcome: the trader can finally answer the question “who are you, financially?” with a URL. The screenshot economy ends. Finance can read his record without him having to convince it.

F·06 Platform self-audit · Archio audited by its own members · published quarterly
The platform itself audited by its own members — the rules Archio applies to mentors, applied to Archio
quarterly self-audit · member-elected board · deviations published in plain English
The break

Every platform that promises trust eventually betrays it — quietly, over a Tuesday, in a config file. The user finds out months later. The platform applies its rules to others and exempts itself.

The moment
Q3 self-audit · published Friday 09:00 UTC · 11 deviations · 4 paid from bond · 1 journalist on the board

Friday 09:00 UTC. Archio publishes its Q3 self-audit. Eleven deviations. Three are model calibration drift — the Forecast surface returned EVs that diverged from realised P&L by more than its stated tolerance on three weeks; corrective action: re-baseline, deadline next Friday, refunds processed for affected users from the bond. Four are refund-rate breaches — disputes resolved more slowly than the published 7-day promise; the bond paid out $11,400 to the affected members. Two are feature drift — the Strategy Engine quietly changed how it weights “consistency” without flagging it; rolled back, public log appended. One is a CEO-disclosure addendum, one a roadmap deferral. The member-elected board signs the report. A journalist who sits on it publishes her dissent on item six, in plain English, in the same document. The next quarter is already calendared. Trust became a receipt with a date on it.

  1. Self-audit charter

    publishes the rules Archio applies to mentors (A·01) and to itself, side by side. commits to applying both equally.

  2. Member board

    elects a rotating member-board with bonded mentors, journalists, and a regulator observer. seats them with read-access to the platform’s own ledger.

  3. Quarterly review

    publishes a quarterly self-audit: feature drift, rule drift, refund stats, dispute outcomes, model calibration drift. refuses to redact for marketing.

  4. Deviation report

    names deviations in plain English and the reason for them. commits a corrective action and a deadline. publishes failures to meet it.

  5. Whistle-blow

    permits any member to file a structured whistle-blow. routes through the dispute panel (A·06), with the platform as the respondent.

  6. Bond

    posts a public bond against its own conduct. commits to refunding members on validated breach, just as a mentor would.

  7. Sunset clause

    publishes a clear data-portability and account-deletion path. commits that the trader’s ledger leaves with him, signed, exportable, on his ownership.

What is being repaired

Every platform that promises trust eventually betrays it — quietly, over a Tuesday, in a config file. The user finds out months later, often only because something stops working the way they remember. The trust is not really betrayed at that moment; it was betrayed every day the platform did not check itself, and the slow betrayal was invisible until it accumulated. Members learn, over years, to expect this curve and to discount platform promises accordingly. The rational response — assume drift — becomes the default emotional posture, and every product surface is read through it.

A published quarterly self-audit, with a member-elected board, a real bond, and a journalist who can dissent in the same document, makes betrayal observable. The platform stands inside the same governance it imposes on mentors. Trust becomes a receipt with a date on it, not a sentence on a marketing page. Once members see one cycle complete — deviations named, bond paid out, corrections shipped on the deadline — they stop wondering whether the next one will arrive. They read it. The credible threat of being audited by its own members is what keeps every other chain on this page true.

Before / after

  • Trust asslogan→quarterly receipt
  • Rules applyto mentors only→equally to Archio
  • When members find driftmonths later→the quarter it happened

One feature, one chain, one outcome: the platform stands inside the same governance it imposes on the rest. The credible threat of being audited by its own members is what keeps the rest of the chains true. The trust isn’t a slogan; it’s a published quarterly receipt.

Six bands. Thirty-six breaks. Thirty-six features. Thirty-six closed loops. Each chain above is one product, doing one job, on one side of the room. Nobody is being “empowered.” Nothing is being “unlocked.” A specific failure in today’s stack is being answered by a specific feature, in the specific sequence the feature runs, on the specific surface that owns it. This is the shape of every slide on Archio, every feature page, every onboarding flow, every pricing line. If the feature cannot be drawn as a chain like this — break in two lines, product answer in seven beats, outcome in one sentence — we do not ship it.

Your stop is checked against the historical hunt-zone for the instrument before fill, not after the print. The release clock ticks on the order pane, not in a browser tab twelve windows deep. You stop holding through news by accident. The decision to hold is now a decision, not a forgetting. The stop no longer sits in the statistically-predictable hunt zone because Cockpit refuses to place it there without you acknowledging it explicitly.
Twitter / X Fin-Twit timeline + screenshots of other traders’ winners nothing — deliberately X is not replaced. X is removed from the loop. Archio does not pipe a firehose of strangers’ confidence into your session, and will not. If Network has nothing to say, Network stays quiet. The mentor speaks; the room does not shout. You stop importing other people’s confidence into your nervous system. The +4R stranger’s screenshot does not reach your size. The sentiment loop that costs you 2–3 R-multiples a week in over-sizing simply disappears.
Telegram signal groups + paid calls + “VIP” rooms also nothing — deliberately Signal channels are not replaced. Signals are the opposite of what Archio is built to do — somebody else’s levels, somebody else’s reasons, somebody else’s confidence. The Network surface holds your own verified mentor, not a stranger broadcasting into eleven thousand traders at once. You stop chasing. The 41%-hit-rate channel stops costing you $49 a month. Your win rate on trades you planned becomes visible. The phrase “it wasn’t my setup” leaves your review.
Your own willpower + sticky notes + “I’ll do better tomorrow” + a Post-it on the monitor that says “wait for setup.” all six surfaces, together Discipline stops being a personal trait you have to summon at 11:42 and becomes a property of the system. The platform itself remembers what you agreed to — so in the one second your will is weakest, there is a second, third, fourth, and fifth opinion already in the room, pre-agreed to by you, standing between your click and the broker. You stop relying on a tired version of yourself to enforce rules a rested version of yourself wrote. The burden of being every role — trader, journal, mentor, psychologist, risk officer — is finally offloaded. You just have to be the trader.
Coffee + Twitter scroll + checking the Discord + reading two mentor videos + guessing how you feel today System OS + Forecast + Network (the pre-bell ritual) One card, thirty seconds to read, handed to you at your desk before the first tick. Today’s psychology read (“you slept 6h, tilt threshold lower”), the strategy note (“rule that broke last Thursday still on probation”), the two instruments the system would not stop you from trading, and the one it would. Signed by your mentor. You stop guessing. The first ten minutes of your session stop being a cold start. You arrive prepared — which was what the Sunday plan was supposed to do and has never once actually done, because the plan was in Notion and Notion does not deliver.
Sunday: 3–5 hours reconciling broker statements, pasting Sheets, re-writing journal entries from memory, watching the recap video, updating the plan nobody will enforce Dashboard AI (reading-only) Sunday review opens to the stamped events, with every beat already there. Every trade has six beats (prep, entry, management, exit, post, review), cryptographically signed. You do not write Sunday; you read Sunday. The week narrates itself. Your Sunday comes back. The $186-a-month, 3–5-hour weekly tax becomes zero. The space you gave to being a bookkeeper is given back to being a trader — or, for the first time in years, to not being a trader at all for one day.
The blunt version

Fourteen surfaces in, one ledger out. You do not get a new product; you get back the hours, the Sundays, the calm, and the space in your head that the stack has been renting for years. The promise is not “we’ll make you a better trader.” The promise is: you will stop being fourteen things at once, and go back to being one.

What happens next
Six parts of the product notice the same click — almost at the same time — and each one does one small thing.
Firstbefore the click even lands
01 System OS
Reads his body, not his story.

He is telling himself “this one’s different.” But his hand is shaky, his breathing is shallow, and he is clicking much faster than he usually does. System OS does not ask how he feels — it simply notices what the body is doing, and quietly writes down one word everyone else on the product will see a split-second later: tired.

Thenhis past answers him
02 Forecast
Checks this moment against every other time he has been here.

He has been in this exact state before — tired, just after losing money, hand hovering over the Buy button. Forecast quietly counts how many times, and how those times went. The answer: thirty-one times. Only a handful ended well. These numbers are his own, not somebody else’s advice. It is very hard to argue with your own numbers.

Nexthis mentor’s voice arrives
03 Network
Surfaces a promise he made to someone he trusts.

On Sunday, his mentor asked him to sign one line: “don’t click again for thirty minutes after a losing trade.” He agreed, three days ago. That sentence, with his mentor’s name on it, appears on the screen now. Not as a warning. Not as a nag. As a reminder of something he already promised — to a person he chose.

A moment laterthe click is held, not stopped
04 Cockpit
Holds the click. Does not cancel it.

Cockpit sees the three things above — the body, the history, the promise — and gently slows the order down. It does not cancel the trade. It does not flash red. A soft line appears under the ticket: “three seconds · type a reason to proceed.” He is still in charge of his money. The product is just asking him to mean it.

Thenone sentence, not a beep
05 Copilot
Writes one sentence, in his voice, with receipts.

Copilot does not shout. It writes one calm sentence at the edge of the screen, with four tiny “why” chips beside it — each one clickable if he wants to argue. The sentence reads something like: “Your hand is shaky, most times you have been here it hasn’t gone well, and you promised your mentor you would wait. Take the three seconds, then decide.” No alarm. No exclamation mark. Four small receipts if he wants to push back.

Finallythe moment is kept
06 Dashboard AI
Remembers this moment, so he does not have to.

Whatever he does next — cancel, proceed, walk away — every part of this moment is saved. The five things you just read, the reminder, the sentence, his final choice. On Sunday, when he sits down to review his week, this moment is the first scene waiting for him, exactly as it happened. He does not have to write it down. The product already did.

What he sees on his screen
Nothing dramatic. One soft line. Three seconds.

No pop-up. No red colours. No shame. A single calm line under the button, with four small why chips he can click if he disagrees. He can press Escape to cancel, type three words to proceed anyway, or do nothing and the order quietly disappears. He is still in charge. The product has just made sure he could see the whole picture before he moved.

What the product now keeps
This moment, in full. For as long as he uses it.

Whatever he chooses — cancel, proceed, step away — every part of this moment is kept: his mood, his history, the promise, the sentence, his final choice. It cannot be edited, and he can always export it. On Sunday, when he reviews his week, this is the first scene waiting for him. He does not have to remember. The product already does.

Why it works
This moment works on a human, not on a screen.

Each of the six catches above is aimed at one very specific human thing — the kind of thing every person, not just a trader, does when they are tired and under pressure. One reminder rarely holds against a tired mind. Six, arriving almost together, almost always do. Below is what each of the six is really for.

Why · 01
The body moves before the mind can think.

When a person is rattled, their hand starts moving before the part of the mind that decides catches up. By the time he tells himself “wait,” the click is already half-done. System OS watches the body instead of asking the mind — and notices the rattle before the click even finishes.

Catch 01 · body before story
Why · 02
It is easier to argue with your own numbers.

A tired mind over-weights whatever just happened. What cools it down is not a lecture — it is a larger, colder look at his own history. Thirty-one times he has been here. He recognises every one of them. You cannot argue with yourself the way you argue with an app.

Catch 02 · his own past, shown back to him
Why · 03
A promise he made is harder to break than a rule the app imposes.

A rule an app invents is easy to ignore. A promise he made to a person he chose, three days ago, is much harder. Network is not bossing him around — it is reminding him of something he already signed, with the face of the person he signed it with.

Catch 03 · past self, speaking back
Why · 04
A pause is easier to accept than a “no”.

When a person is wound up, being told “no” makes them tighter. Being told “in three seconds, if you still want to” relaxes them. Cockpit does not fight him. It just asks him to wait for three breaths. That is the only kind of friction a tired person will accept.

Catch 04 · wait, don’t refuse
Why · 05
A sentence you can argue with is trusted more than an alarm.

An alarm feels like a parent. A sentence that explains itself feels like a colleague. People rebel against parents; they discuss things with colleagues. Copilot never gives orders — it shows its reasoning, lets him disagree, and quietly records the disagreement. Over weeks, that builds trust.

Catch 05 · sentence, not siren
Why · 06
A mind forgets. The product does not.

On Sunday, his memory of Tuesday will be a feeling, not a fact. That is the weakest link in getting better. Dashboard AI quietly keeps the whole moment — his mood, his history, the reminder, his final choice — so Sunday review becomes reading the week back, not trying to remember it.

Catch 06 · memory kept for him
Production constraints
Hard rules. The demo ships, or we redesign it until it does.
  1. Zero backend, zero signup, zero telemetry leaving the client. All six beats are canned timelines bound to one hardcoded scene file. The marketing page does not read the product.
  2. Under 420ms total, 60fps throughout. Motion budget: two simultaneous transforms max, all easing on a single curve. The cockpit demo must feel like the cockpit, not a Lottie.
  3. Fully keyboard navigable. Arrow keys step between beats. Enter opens any why chip. Escape closes. Focus order matches reading order.
  4. Respects prefers-reduced-motion. With the OS flag on, all six beats cross-fade in place. No translation. No scale. The information arrives; the motion doesn’t.
  5. Static fallback without JavaScript. The scene renders as a single, beautiful, editorial diagram — the same six beats, laid out as a printed page. The demo is the page itself, not a script tag.
  6. Copy is frozen by a trader, not a copywriter. Every sentence in every beat is ghostwritten with a profitable trader and signed off before build. No synonyms. No "elevate." No "empower." Trader voice only.

Five rules we hold ourselves to

The pitch, in five lines.

Everything the nine-app stack gets wrong in the ten moments below comes from breaking one of five rules. We wrote these down before we wrote a line of product. If a rule is ever broken in production, a public post-mortem ships within the next release cycle — no reddit thread required.

Signed · v1.0 Operational, not aspirational. Post-mortems Public within one release cycle.
Rule · 01

We never invent data.

Under-sampled means under-sampled. We say so, we shut up, and we never colour the chart to hide it.

If Forecast can’t pull at least 10 analogous events, the EV chip shows “n < 10” in the same spot a number would go, and Copilot defaults to wait. Every statistic carries sample size and confidence interval; below the statistical floor the card is blank and the engine is silent. No fabricated confidence, no “AI says so” without receipts.

Applies to: 03 · 07 · 08
Rule · 02

We never write your feelings.

We capture what is measurable. Meaning stays with you. Commitments are private until you share them.

Dashboard AI pre-fills only what the ledger can prove — price, size, time, rule-state, body-state. Human interpretation lives in blank fields with questions, not guesses. Psych Analyzer never turns a highlighted paragraph into a public callout; consent is per event, not per account. Every capture is exportable and deletable on request, including audit records.

Applies to: 02 · 05 · 06
Rule · 03

We never block silently.

Every hold shows the exact number that would release it. Every interlock cites its own rule, verbatim.

Cockpit never refuses an order without rendering, inline: the rule being enforced, the projected breach number, and the exact size/stop that would clear it. Every hold is auditable millisecond by millisecond, with server-side timestamps the user cannot forge. Overrides are signed paragraphs, not silent checkboxes; cancels are never silent.

Applies to: 01 · 04 · 09
Rule · 04

We never moralise.

No lecture after a winner. No shame after a loss. Citations, not sermons.

Every behavioural flag cites your own rule, in your own words, with the timestamp you wrote it. If you never wrote the rule, Cockpit shows a neutral probability figure and leaves the judgement alone — we will not impose a prior you didn’t sign. Bias flags are muteable per session, and every mute is logged with its reason so you can audit yourself, not so we can audit you.

Applies to: 04 · 06 · 09
Rule · 05

We compete on receipts.

Discord stays open. We just surface your own history faster than the chat can pull you off the plan.

We will not hide tabs, throttle notifications, or gamify presence. When System OS catches a validation-seeking tab switch, Copilot surfaces your own last 8 trades of the same setup in 300 ms — with invalidation, hold time, and R-outcome cited. If your own receipts on this setup are worse than the chat’s opinion, we say so in the same card. The Copilot will cite you against you when the data demands it.

Applies to: 07 · 10
These are the five. Everything that follows — the ten moments, the six surfaces, the forty-eight modules — is how we honour them in production. If any moment below meets a rule broken, the page breaks with it.

08 Three Doors, One Commercial Surface

Three doors. Two places to meet them. The only place this site asks for anything.

Every visitor to Archio is one of three people. A beginner — not yet in the stack. A growing trader — in the stack and breaking under it. A mentor or leader — already running a room, needing audit and amplification. Each gets his own onboarding world, his own questions, his own AI-brain tuning. The doors into these worlds appear in exactly two places on the public site: at the close of the landing (after the disconnect has been felt, the order has been formed, the six surfaces have been named), and at the close of every feature page (after the seven-beat arc has done its work). Same three boxes. Same three URLs. Copy rewritten per surface so the invitation matches what the reader was just reading. This chapter is the specification of those three worlds and, just as importantly, the specification of where the doors appear and where they must not.

The placement contract

Where the doors live. Where the doors never live.

The doors live at the close of the landing…
…as the final beat, directly under the feature-index (Movement III). The reader has walked through the disconnect, watched the order form, seen the six surfaces name themselves — and is now handed the three boxes. Beginner. Growing trader. Mentor · Leader. Each is a door to a separate onboarding world. This is the sign-up on the landing. It is not above the fold, not in the hero, not in the nav. It is earned by the scroll.
The doors also live at the close of every feature page…
…as beat 07 of the seven-beat arc. Six feature pages, one door trio each, same shape every time. The door copy is rewritten per surface so the beginner’s reason to enter through Copilot is not the same sentence as his reason to enter through Network. The three URLs are the same; the invitation is not.
The doors never live anywhere else…
…no sticky CTA strip on scroll, no nav-level “Sign up” button, no email capture in the hero, no exit-intent modal, no mid-scroll interstitials. If a visitor wants to sign up before the page has earned it, we want that friction — we want him to keep reading first. The argument comes before the invitation.
Also not allowed…
…a /pricing page. A /signup shortcut. A generic “Get Started” anywhere. The site has exactly three signup URLs — /start/beginner, /start/grower, /start/mentor — and they are reachable only by walking through one of the two permitted door trios (landing close or feature-page close). The door is the signup. The referring surface is tracked and tunes the onboarding world the reader lands in (see Ch 14 onboarding wireframes).
In plain English

Two places. Same three boxes. Always at the close of a read, never at the open. A trader who reads the landing top-to-bottom meets the doors once. A trader who opens the Copilot feature page meets them again, but with Copilot-specific copy. A trader who opens Network meets them again, with Network-specific copy. Every door trio hands him the same three URLs — and the system remembers which page he came from, so the onboarding world opens to the tour that fits what he was just reading.

Door 01 · Beginner

I am just starting.

Has not placed a real trade, or has placed a few and lost them. Has not yet assembled the nine-app stack from Ch 02, and does not want to. What he needs: a slower room, a verified mentor, an AI copilot that explains every intervention, and a first-win framing that is a rule kept, not a dollar won.

"Start where the best traders already are."
Walks into/start/beginner
Door 02 · Growing trader

I am already trading.

Already inside the nine-app stack. Has a broker, a journal, a Discord or two, a prop-firm dashboard. Knows the language. Is here because the manual force of holding it together is breaking him. What he needs: import first, edge decomposition, and an AI brain that speaks in trader shorthand, not first-principles.

"Know the edge you have. Repeat the edge you know."
Walks into/start/grower
Door 03 · Mentor · Leader

I teach. I lead a room.

Verified mentor, prop-firm head of trading, desk lead, or educator with a track record. Runs a live room or a cohort. Wants to be audited, paid fairly, and not chained to live hours. What is behind the door · the onboarding world, in full

A door is easy. The world behind it is where the promise gets paid.

The card you just clicked is a door, and every door opens onto a completely separate onboarding world at /start/… — its own welcome tone, its own questions, its own first-tour, its own AI-brain tuning. Below is the full spec of that world: the intake, the routes, the matches, the curriculum, the covenant. Every word is a responsibility we accept on day one. The wireframes for these worlds live in Ch 14 · The Blueprint; this chapter is the narrative behind those wireframes.

02 / 06

Two routes, one combined. You choose; we honour the choice.

Mentor · AI · both

Based on your intake, Archio proposes one of three routes. Every route is self-contained — you do not need to buy a mentor to get the AI, and you do not need the AI to get a mentor. If you want both, the product assumes that by default and gets cheaper.

R 01 Human-led
Matched to a verified beginner-friendly community.

We read your intake and pair you with two or three vetted rooms inside Archio that actively take learners at your level. No cold Discord. No influencer traps. Each mentor has a signed track-record audit visible on their room page.

  • Mentor is KYC'd & audited by Archio
  • Room owner agrees to the Learner Covenant
  • First week free · then member rate
  • Full Archio Copilot included while you’re a member
from $19 / mo · varies by mentor
R 02 AI-led
Archio Tutor — self-paced, adaptive, ours to own.

If you prefer to learn alone, Tutor is the curriculum we take full responsibility for. It tests you, corrects you, drills you, and refuses to let you move past a concept you have not demonstrated. No human mentor required.

  • 12-module curriculum · 60–90 hrs
  • Adaptive to your session length & pace
  • Live drills on your own sim account
  • Weekly progress report, signed
$29 / mo · cancel anytime
R 03 Combined
Mentor & Tutor, running in parallel.

The default for most learners. Tutor builds the foundation on your own time; the mentor’s live room brings context, accountability, and humans. Neither fights the other — they share the same record of what you already know.

  • Tutor + any matched community room
  • Mentor sees your Tutor progress (with consent)
  • One bill, 20 % off the combined rate
  • Graduation flag when Tutor is complete
from $39 / mo · combined

04 / 06

Archio Tutor · the feature that takes responsibility for your education.

Full-stack AI curriculum

Tutor is not a chatbot. It is a curriculum with a mandate: if you finish its 12 modules, you can describe an edge, run a plan, and read a chart. If you do not finish, Tutor is free. We accept the downside of that claim because the feature is designed to earn it.

The mandate
By the end of module twelve, you can name your edge, size a trade, and run a two-week review — alone, without us.

Tutor reads your intake, starts you at the right module, and never lets you skip. Every module has a live drill on your sim account that is marked by the system, not by you. If you fail a drill, the next module is locked until you pass.

If you hit module twelve and still cannot describe your edge in one sentence, Tutor refunds the last three months and auto-escalates you to a mentor match at no cost. This is written into the feature, not the marketing.

Responsibility 1
Adaptivity

Sessions compress or expand around your weekly hours; the 12 modules never stretch beyond 16 weeks without an explicit opt-in.

Responsibility 2
Honest gating

No skip-ahead. No “mark as read.” Every gate closes behind a demonstrated behaviour on a sim account, not a quiz answer.

Responsibility 3
Handover on demand

At any point, one click hands your full Tutor progress to a matched mentor with your signed consent — they pick up where we left off.

Responsibility 4
The refund clause

If a learner finishes and still cannot describe their edge, Tutor refunds the last 90 days. This is the clause that keeps the product honest.

No crippled subsets.

The growth stack, surface by surface.

Why none of these ship alone

Six surfaces, one memory. Below is the responsibility each surface takes inside the stack, the upstream input that makes its job possible, and the downstream surface that consumes its output. If a surface is removed, the two it feeds stop being themselves — that is the literal reason we do not sell pieces.

F 01 Copilot
Writes the cited verdict.

One sentence at the edge of the screen, in your voice, with four why-chips each clickable to the raw signal that produced it — never a generic LLM answer.

  • Reads from · F02 edge name, F04 confluences, F05 EV, F03 psychology state
  • Feeds · F06 Sunday review, every ledger entry, every contract trigger
Ships in the stack · not sold alone
F 02 Strategy Engine
Names your edge in one line.

Decomposes your trade history into the two or three setups that actually carry your P&L — or writes “no edge named” if the data refuses to produce one.

  • Reads from · ledger import, F04 confluences, broker statement
  • Feeds · F01 Copilot voice, F05 Forecast similarity, F06 weekly arc
Ships in the stack · not sold alone
F 03 Psychology Analyzer
Reports your tilt patterns.

Cross-references body signal (HRV, click cadence) with outcome and rule violations — tells you which hour of which day you break, and why.

  • Reads from · wearables, click telemetry, F02 rule book
  • Feeds · F01 Copilot warnings, F06 review tone, room alerts
Ships in the stack · not sold alone
F 04 Confluences
Reads which factors co-occur on your winners.

Not a strategy. A query engine over your own history: “when X and Y are true, how do I actually perform on this instrument?” Cited answers, never invented patterns.

  • Reads from · full ledger, F02 setups, market context
  • Feeds · F01 Copilot reasons, F05 Forecast inputs, F06 review themes
Ships in the stack · not sold alone
F 05 Forecast
Returns your personal EV, in R.

Pulls the 31 most-similar trades from your own ledger and returns the cited expected value before you click. Every R is traceable to a real prior trade, not a backtest.

  • Reads from · F02 setup tag, F04 confluences, F03 state
  • Feeds · F01 Copilot verdict, the order ticket, F06 outcome record
Ships in the stack · not sold alone
F 06 Dashboard AI
Writes your Sunday review before you open it.

Appends every beat — entry, exit, rule, body state, mentor contract — to the ledger, then opens the review pre-written, citing the week’s edge, tilt, and the next focus.

  • Reads from · every other surface, F01 through F05
  • Feeds · F02 next week’s edge frame, F03 next week’s tilt watch
Ships in the stack · not sold alone
Why no à la carte
Each of the six is the input to two others.

Copilot without Confluences is a generic LLM. Forecast without Strategy Engine is a backtest of nobody. Psychology Analyzer without Copilot is a journal entry. Dashboard AI without all five is a Sunday email. Cherry-picking the stack is what every other journaling tool already sells, and it is exactly the failure that put nine apps on the trader’s desktop in the first place. One memory, six surfaces, one price.

04 / 06

The friends room · eight seats, eight agents.

2 – 8 traders · one personalised agent each

Most growing traders do not need a mentor; they need two or three trusted people running their own strategy, side by side. Archio makes that first-class: each seat keeps the full six-surface stack and gets its own personalised AI agent and dashboard — not a shared chatbot, not a single account everyone logs into. The room layer is what they share. The brain is private to each friend.

What’s inside
Eight private cockpits, one shared room.

Each seat ships with its own Copilot voice, own ledger, own psychology profile, own Dashboard AI, own Sunday review. Marco’s agent learns Marco. Aria’s agent learns Aria. Neither agent ever speaks for the other; neither dashboard is shared. The friends room sits on top of those eight private cockpits as a thin social layer — the rule book they all signed, the watchlist they all read, the equity curve that pools the eight ledgers, and a voice channel for the times screens are not enough.

Psychology alerts cross seats only with explicit, revocable consent: if Marco tilts at 96 bpm and has opted in, Aria sees a quiet flag in the room sidebar — not the chart, not the size, not the trade. Just “Marco at threshold.” Friends, not surveillance.

No mentor. No auditor. No public listing. You are the room. If two of the eight want to leave and start their own, they can, and their agent + dashboard + ledger go with them — intact.

Per-seat brain
One personalised agent per friend

Each seat’s agent is trained only on that trader’s ledger, voice, hours, rules, and body data. No shared model. No cross-pollination unless the trader explicitly publishes a rule into the room.

Per-seat dashboard
Your dashboard is yours

Each friend keeps their own Dashboard AI, their own Sunday review, their own confluences view. The shared room view is a separate surface — never replaces the personal one.

Shared room layer
Rule book · watchlist · pooled curve

One signed rule book across the seats. One shared watchlist. One pooled equity curve that respects per-seat privacy by default. Voice channel · replay · clip-to-ledger, all on-platform.

Cross-seat psychology
Consent-gated, revocable

Tilt alerts cross seats only when each seat opts in. The alert is a flag, not the trade. Consent can be revoked any second; the flag stops in real time.

Capacity
Hard-capped at 8 seats

Enforced at the product level. If you want more, you open a Leading-path community, not a bigger friends room.

Billing
$49 per seat · full stack each

Every seat pays the full-stack price; nothing is locked behind “room admin.” The room owner can absorb seats if they want; billing is flexible, the per-seat stack is not.

Exit
Agent + data leave with you

If a friend leaves, their personalised agent, their dashboard, their ledger, their psychology profile export in full. No lock-in. No “room data is ours.”

Upgrade
Graduate to Leading

Outgrew eight seats? One click turns your friends room into a vetted, KYC’d Leading-path community, with each seat’s history and agent intact.

01 / 06

The gate. Hard KYC, human review, Archio Pro status.

Not self-serve

The Leading path is the only non-self-serve path in Archio. You apply. We verify. We audit. We approve. The reason is simple: learners and growers are matched to mentors on our platform, and we are the only thing standing between them and a Discord con artist with a Photoshop track record.

Archio Pro · earned, not bought.
Application required

Every Archio Pro is hard-KYC’d, identity-verified, and has their track record audited from the broker statement, not the screenshot. The badge is quarterly-refreshed. If the audit lapses, the badge disappears and the matched learners are rerouted — automatically.

02 / 06

The application, five stages.

~3 weeks end-to-end

The application is a pipeline, not a form. Each stage has a clear pass criterion and a clear pass rate. Most applications take two to three weeks. We reject more than we accept — on purpose.

Stage 01
Identity & KYC

Government ID, proof of address, selfie-liveness. Run through our compliance partner. No anonymous mentors on this platform, ever.

48 hrs · ~95 % pass
Stage 02
Track record audit

We read the broker statements you upload. Not the Discord screenshots. Three years minimum, or two with a verified prop history.

5–7 days · ~45 % pass
Stage 03
Pedagogy review

Two Archio reviewers sit in on two of your recorded calls or classes. We grade for clarity, safety, and honesty — not hype.

3–5 days · ~60 % pass
Stage 04
Covenant & contract

You sign the Archio Pro Covenant: audit cadence, refund policy, data-exit promise, and code of conduct. Non-negotiable.

1–2 days · ~100 %
Stage 05
Room launch

Room opens with 10 invited learners. AI agent of yourself is trained on your materials. The audit badge goes live. You are an Archio Pro.

immediate · ~100 %

Learning · what this is NOT
Not a "trade my signals" room.
  • Not a signal service. We do not tell you what to buy. If you wanted that, this is not the path.
  • Not a shortcut. Tutor takes 12 modules and will not let you skip. The work is the point.
  • Not a prop-firm affiliate. We do not take commission on prop evaluations. We are not paid to send you to one.
  • Not a Discord expansion. The matched rooms are on-platform, not another Discord you already do not read.
  • Not a “guaranteed profitable” scheme. Trading is hard. We make it learnable, not easy.
Growing · what this is NOT
Not a mentor-or-nothing bundle.
  • Not à la carte. The six surfaces ship as one because each one is the input to two others. Cherry-picking is what every other journaling tool sells; it is precisely the failure we exist to fix.
  • Not a shared room brain. A friends room is eight private cockpits sharing a rule book — not eight people logged into one chatbot. Every seat keeps its own agent and dashboard.
  • Not a public community. Friends rooms are hard-capped at 8; there is no “scale your room to 500” upgrade path here.
  • Not a signal AI. Copilot cites your own history. It does not tell you what to buy. It tells you whether to fire.
  • Not a vanity dashboard. If the Strategy Engine cannot find your edge, it writes “no edge named,” not a flattering report.
  • Not a lock-in. Cancel, export, leave. Your ledger, strategy doc, and personalised agent travel with you.
Leading · what this is NOT
Not a "creator program" badge.
  • Not self-serve. You cannot buy your way into Pro. It is audited, reviewed, and voted on by two humans.
  • Not cosmetic. The badge is earned on broker statements, not on follower count. It drops if audits lapse.
  • Not Discord with extra steps. Your room runs on Archio, not on a chat app with a pinned PDF.
  • Not a rug-pull contract. The 15 % fee is fixed in writing. 90-day notice on any change. 180-day sunset if we ever move.
  • Not unlimited upside for us. We will not run competing-mentor ads inside your room. Ever.
Learning · FAQ
What happens if I cannot commit 10 hours a week?

Tutor adapts: its 12 modules compress or expand around your weekly hours, and the matched communities include an explicit "under 10 hrs / wk" tier. You will not be forced into a pace that breaks you.

Do I have to pick a mentor?

No. Route 02 is AI-only — Archio Tutor takes full responsibility for your curriculum without a human mentor. If you finish the 12 modules and still cannot name your edge, Tutor refunds 90 days, automatically.

Who are the mentors, really?

KYC’d humans with signed, broker-statement-verified track records that refresh every 90 days. Not Twitter anons. Not Lambo thumbnails. If an audit lapses, the match breaks and you are re-routed.

When do I graduate?

When your ledger shows three consecutive rule-compliant weeks on sim. A graduation flag appears in your account and the Growing door unlocks. You do not have to move; but it opens.

Growing · FAQ
Why can’t I buy just Copilot, or just Confluences?

Because Copilot without Confluences is a generic LLM, and Confluences without Strategy Engine is a query engine over an unnamed edge. Each of the six surfaces is the input to two others — remove one and the next two stop being themselves. The stack ships whole at $49 / mo, full export at exit, 30-day refund if no edge is named.

What is the friends room, exactly?

Two to eight traders, private, each with their own personalised AI agent and their own dashboard. The shared layer is the rule book, the watchlist, the pooled equity curve, and consent-gated tilt alerts. Not a shared chatbot — eight private cockpits, one shared room. $49 / seat / mo, full stack per seat, no room surcharge.

Does each friend really get their own agent?

Yes. Marco’s Copilot trains on Marco’s ledger, Marco’s rules, Marco’s hours, Marco’s body data. Aria’s trains on Aria’s. Neither agent ever speaks for the other. If a friend leaves the room, their agent + dashboard + ledger export with them, intact. The shared layer is the room, not the brain.

Can I sell my dashboard without a community?

Yes. Route 03 lets you list a dashboard or an AI agent of yourself in the marketplace at 15 % platform fee. No KYC gate at this tier. You keep 85 %, and Archio handles hosting, billing, and the disclosure that buyers are talking to your agent — not you.

What if Strategy Engine cannot find my edge?

Then it says so, in writing. The feature will not invent a flattering narrative. If 90 days of trades produce no nameable edge, you get a refund and a one-on-one session with an Archio analyst, free.

Leading · FAQ
How hard is the application really?

Hard on purpose. Stage 02 (track-record audit) has a ~45 % pass rate; Stage 03 (pedagogy review) is another ~60 %. End-to-end, roughly one in four applicants becomes a Pro. The rejection is the product.

What is the fee, exactly?

A flat 15 % of your room’s monthly revenue. Nothing else. No "creator fund" skimming, no surprise tiers. The rate is fixed in the Pro contract with 90-day written notice required for any change.

Do I own my audience?

Yes. Member list, DMs, recordings, announcements — all exportable any time. If Archio ever sunsets your tier, we give you 180 days and the full export. Not 30 days and a Discord link.

What is the AI agent of me, really?

A model trained on your own materials — your videos, pinned rules, FAQ. It answers members when you are asleep. It always cites you, never impersonates. Users see clearly when they are talking to the agent.

§
09 The Extension Concept

The landing is an index. Every surface is a volume. Every volume ends at the doors.

We are not building a landing page with a feature grid. We are building the front page of a publication where every surface has its own full-length page of the same editorial caliber. When the reader clicks a surface from the landing’s feature index, he opens its page — indistinguishable from the landing in design and voice. Every feature page obeys the same seven-beat arc and ends at the same three doors. The seven beats are the same on every page so the reader learns the shape once. The three doors are the same three doors on every page so the signup is never in doubt, and the copy inside each door is rewritten per surface so the reason to enter is never generic.

The feature-page shape — seven beats, three doors.

Every feature page obeys this exact shape. This is what makes six different pages feel like six volumes of one library:

  1. 01 · Entry. The sigil, the surface number, the surface name, the one-line frame. No hero image. No CTA. The page breathes in. (Wireframe: Ch 14 · feature page · beat 01.)
  2. 02 · Today. Two to three paragraphs describing what the trader does right now without this surface — in his own words, zero solution language. Taken from Ch 03 (the current reality) and Ch 05 (the scenes).
  3. 03 · Replaces. The rows from the landing’s replacement map that apply to this surface — same three columns, same wording: was · is now · gain. If a surface replaces one app, one row. If it replaces three, three rows.
  4. 04 · Different. The mechanism. One paragraph, then one live demo inline wherever the surface supports it. This is where the page earns its claim that the old stack cannot do this.
  5. 05 · Connects. The same wiring diagram as the landing’s Movement II flow — but visually centred on the surface the reader is on. The emphasis shifts; the structure does not. This is the beat that makes the network visible on every page.
  6. 06 · Modules. The surface’s own sub-modules. Each module gets a sentence, not a page. (This is where Ch 10’s per-feature content is split.)
  7. 07 · Who it is for · The three doors. The only commercial surface on the page. Three cards of equal weight — Beginner, Growing trader, Mentor · Leader — with copy rewritten for this surface: what Copilot does for a beginner is not what Copilot does for a mentor, and the door reflects that. Clicking a door walks the reader into the matching onboarding world at /start/beginner, /start/grower, or /start/mentor. There is no seventh option. There is no “Sign up” button. The door is the signup. See Ch 08 · the placement contract.

Every feature page ships with its own URL (/feature/network, /feature/cockpit, /feature/system-os, /feature/forecast, /feature/copilot, /feature/dashboard-ai), its own OG image, and its own meta description, so that a serious trader can link to it on its own and have it land with editorial weight on its own. The feature page is not a subordinate of the landing; it is a sibling. The doors at its foot are the only place the reader can sign up, and they are on every sibling, so any path through the site lands the reader at the right door for who he is.

“In five years, a prop firm operator will paste you a link to a single Archio feature page the way a lawyer pastes you a link to a single journal article.”

— Long-term thesis, platform docs

FEATURE · 01

Unified Network

/archio/network

The first structured trading network on the public internet. A real floor, not a chat server. Verified mentors. Recorded calls. An AI agent of every mentor available 24/7. A room-finder that places you with traders your size and style. No gurus, no rugs, no silence when the market moves.

He currently lives like this

He pays $250 a month to a Discord run by a man he has never verified. The call starts at 8am. He is on a train at 8am. The call is not recorded. The chat is 4,000 messages deep by 10am. Nobody answers him when his trade goes wrong. The mentor sleeps. The Discord never audits anyone. He is the product.

Archio does this

Every room is audited. Every mentor is verified. Every call is recorded and transcribed. Every mentor has an AI agent, trained on his voice and archive, that answers students 24/7 while he sleeps. The community finder matches him to a room by style, not by wallet.

How it is different

The AI agent of the mentor is a first: it knows what the mentor has said, across every call, every trade, every message, and can answer a student in the mentor's voice when the mentor is not awake. The agent is not hallucinating; it is citing.

LOGIC

How a trader joins a room

Six steps, in order. The room governs itself. Archio governs the room.

  1. 01
    Arrive

    The trader lands on the Community Finder — a radial map of every verified room. No paid placements. Filters: asset class, trade style, session window, room size, mentor verification tier.

  2. 02
    Match

    Archio reads the trader's own profile — his DNA (scalper / swing / hybrid), his hours, his discipline score — and ranks rooms by fit, not by the mentor's ad budget. The match is a score, 0–100, with the reasons shown.

  3. 03
    Verify

    Every mentor carries a public audit card: tier (Emerging / Established / Anchor), months verified, live-account attestation, strategy disclosure, disciplinary history. The trader sees all four before he sees a price.

  4. 04
    Enter

    Joining a room is instant. The trader's profile carries into the room — his DNA, his rule commitments, his active positions. The mentor can see him as a whole trader, not as a silent green dot in Discord.

  5. 05
    Trade

    Every live call is recorded, transcribed, and frame-stamped with the market. Every chat message is linked to the price at which it was sent. Every tag of the AI agent is logged with the mentor's source calls.

  6. 06
    Grow

    The mentor sees each student's progression as a curve, not a testimonial. Students graduate. Rooms evolve. The mentor is rewarded for traders who graduate, not for traders who pay another month.

PILLAR · I
Verification Ladder

Four public tiers. Every mentor starts at the bottom. Every mentor's tier is visible on his room card and his profile. No tier can be bought.

  1. Tier 0 · Applicant. Unverified. Cannot charge.
  2. Tier 1 · Emerging. Six months of live-account audit. Strategy disclosed.
  3. Tier 2 · Established. Eighteen months + student outcomes verified.
  4. Tier 3 · Anchor. Multi-year record, disciplinary clean, recognised by the floor.
PILLAR · II
Live Call Kernel

The live call is the heart of the room. Archio rebuilds it from scratch so no retail tool has ever seen a call this searchable.

  1. Recorded. Audio + video + chart. Always.
  2. Transcribed. Speaker-diarised. Every sentence is searchable within 60s of being said.
  3. Price-stamped. Every line of speech is linked to the market tick at which it was said.
  4. Indexed. By ticker, by setup, by emotion detected, by rule cited.
PILLAR · III
AI Mentor Agent

The mentor asleep is still the mentor. His agent is trained on every call, every message, every trade he has ever posted — and cites them by timestamp.

  1. Voice-matched. Tone, phrasing, opinions on named setups.
  2. Cited. Every answer links to the call and timestamp it is drawn from.
  3. Boundaried. The agent will refuse to answer what the mentor has never covered.
  4. Reviewed. The mentor can approve, revise, or retire any answer from his dashboard.
PILLAR · IV
War Room Protocol

Inside the main room are smaller rooms the mentor opens for a session, an event, a cohort. Called war rooms because they are opened and closed around a battle.

  1. Event-bound. CPI print, NFP, earnings window, the London open.
  2. Timed. Opens at T-30, closes at T+60. The room is not a chat that runs forever.
  3. Scoped. Max seat count chosen by the mentor. No ghosts.
  4. Archived. When the room closes, it becomes a playback with the chart replayed alongside.

Inside Unified Network — the full surface list

  1. Community Finder. A radial map of all rooms, filterable by style, size, session window, and verification tier. The trader is matched to rooms, never sold to them.
  2. Verified Mentor Profiles. Every mentor carries a public audit card. Tier, months verified, strategy disclosed, disciplinary history, student outcomes.
  3. Daily Gameplan. Pre-market prep posted by the mentor at a fixed hour each day, live-annotated by the room, timestamped against the open.
  4. Live Call Kernel. Audio, video, and chart, recorded, transcribed, speaker-diarised, and price-stamped within 60 seconds.
  5. Live Call Interaction. During the call, students can tag the AI agent inline for clarification without interrupting the mentor's voice.
  6. AI Mentor Agent. 24/7 access to the mentor's accumulated voice. Cites the specific call, message, or trade for every answer it gives.
  7. Agent Dashboard. The mentor approves, revises, or retires any answer his agent produces. The agent is his voice; he owns it.
  8. War Rooms. Event-bound, timed, scoped breakout rooms inside the larger room. Opened at T-30, closed at T+60.
  9. Mentor Dashboard. Room analytics, student progression curves, AI agent tuning, payouts, and room governance in one surface.
  10. Student Profiles. Every student has a profile visible to his mentor — and to no one else — with his trades, his psychology, his progress.
  11. Audited Track Records. Archio does not take a mentor's word for his P&L. It verifies live-account feeds and publishes the result.
  12. Room Governance. A mentor sets his own rules inside his room, but cannot evade Archio's platform-wide covenants.
  13. Graduation Ledger. When a student becomes consistently profitable, his mentor is rewarded. The incentive is graduation, not monthly rent.
  14. Cross-Room Identity. The trader's DNA, discipline score, and psychology carry with him between rooms. His history is his, not the room's.

F01 · Unified Network
Reality · then Order

The world has mentors.
The world does not have a network.

Every serious trader, today, lives across eight rooms that do not know each other exist. A Telegram with the mentor. A Discord for the community. A Google Meet for the call. A Notion for the playbook. A YouTube for the content. A Stripe for the payment. A Twitter for the signal. A WhatsApp for the voice note. None of them know he traded. None of them paid the mentor on outcome. None of them remember the name of the student a year later.

The Unified Network is the recognition that the retail trading world is an economy without a ledger. Students find mentors by luck. Mentors find students by noise. Nobody tracks anything. Archio is the ledger. Mentor discovery, reputation, session calls, chat, content, execution, payment, and review — on one spine, in one trust model, with one audit log.
