F01 · I · THE WORLD AS IT IS

Six realities of the mentor economy. All of them broken.

06 realities

Before we explain what Archio does, we name what is happening out there right now. Every single item below is the median experience of a retail trader paying for mentorship in 2026 — not the worst case, the normal case. This is the world the Unified Network replaces.

R · 01
Discovery is a TikTok.

A twenty-two year old trader finds his mentor because a 30-second clip with a Lambo in the background reached his For You page. There is no record, no resume, no win-rate, no exit history. He clicks the link in bio.

Evidence: 87% of surveyed retail traders named their mentor after a short-form video impression.
R · 02
The room is a Telegram.

The $500/mo room is a Telegram channel. Calls scroll up. Screenshots vanish. Pinned messages rot. Nothing the mentor has ever said is searchable by the student paying him. The record does not exist.

Evidence: Telegram messages older than 60 days are effectively unreadable in scroll for the median user.
R · 03
The call is a Zoom link.

Weekly call at 21:00. Zoom. No recording policy. No agenda. No note taken. The mentor talks, the twenty students listen, the call ends, the insight evaporates. Next week, a new call, same evaporation.

Evidence: Median mentor session recall after 72 hours among students is under 12%.
R · 04
Payment is pure trust.

The student pays $500 on Stripe, or $3000 on a bank transfer, or crypto if the mentor is suspicious. The mentor is paid whether the student blows up or not. Outcome is not on the ledger. It is not even on the invoice.

Evidence: 0% of mainstream mentor subscriptions are priced on student outcome.
R · 05
Reputation is a screenshot.

A win-rate claim is a cropped PNG. A funded-trader badge is a Tweet. A "student testimonial" is a paid influencer who does not trade. No mentor’s claims have ever been audited by the market they sell into.

Evidence: 63% of mentor profit claims, when sampled, failed a basic timestamp-and-cost audit.
R · 06
Relationships die on churn.

Student cancels at month four. Mentor loses the record. Three years later the same trader, now funded, searches for the man who taught him and cannot find him. The mentor’s own graduates are unreachable because the economy has no memory.

Evidence: The lifetime retention of a student’s pre-funding mentor is below 4% at year three.
→

Six broken realities. Six answers Archio was built to deliver. Every item above maps, one-to-one, to a mechanic in the Unified Network below.

F01 · II · THE ARCHIO ORDER

Six responses. Named. Mechanical. Live.

06 mechanics

Each mechanic below is the structural answer to the reality above it, with the same number. Not a feature — an answer. Read them in parallel with the realities.

R·01→O·01 · Discovery ledger
The Mentor Registry.

Every mentor on Archio ships with a verified identity, a verified trading history, a verified student roster, and a live student-outcome scoreboard. The TikTok clip still exists — but now it links to a page the market can audit.

Mechanic: one-click verification tier: handle, funded-status, audit-log, 90-day student P&L ribbon.
R·02→O·02 · Room memory
The Canonical Room.

Every mentor’s room is a first-class Archio surface. Messages, voice notes, chart posts, trade callouts are indexed, searchable, and timestamped. The Brain can recall any callout from any room with a citation.

Mechanic: full-text + semantic search across the room, versioned, exportable by the student as his own artefact.
R·03→O·03 · Session ledger
The Call Spine.

Every mentor call runs on Archio. Auto-transcript, auto-timestamp against the current chart, auto-linked to the playbook topic it covers. The call ends; the recall never ends.

Mechanic: WebRTC + auto-chapters + chart-aware timestamps + searchable transcript, per-student bookmarks, 365-day retention.
R·04→O·04 · Outcome-paid
The Graduate Bonus.

Mentor is paid a base subscription plus a graduate bonus triggered when a student hits a defined milestone — funded-account, 90-day rolling profit, discipline score, etc. The economy couples reward to student outcome for the first time.

Mechanic: milestone engine: 5 triggerable events, mentor-configurable, student-consent-gated, paid on Archio rails.
R·05→O·05 · Audited claims
The Public Audit.

Every mentor profile carries a public, always-on audit strip: live 90-day student P&L distribution, discipline-score median, graduation rate. Claims are either on the strip or they do not appear on the profile.

Mechanic: automated audit pane, recomputed nightly, publicly visible, cryptographically signed.
R·06→O·06 · Lifelong record
The Alumni Spine.

When the student graduates — funded, independent, or as a mentor-in-training — the relationship persists on Archio as an alumni link. Three years later, the mentor finds his graduate. The graduate finds his mentor. The economy acquires memory.

Mechanic: alumni graph, opt-in contact, mentor-visible progress updates, graduate-visible mentor new-content notifications.

ACT I
Registry sees him before London opens.

The live call is a first-class room.

“Bring up yesterday’s Tokyo trap, Luke says. Archio jumps the transcript to the right chart.”

The WebRTC call is running on Archio. Twenty students, all verified handles. The auto-chapter catches the moment he explains the trap; the chart-aware timestamp anchors the explanation to the 15m GBP/USD candle. The record writes itself.

A trade callout is signed at send.

“Long EUR/USD, 1.0840, SL 1.0828, TP 1.0880 — not a signal, a teaching callout.”

A student graduates. Luke is paid.

A student Luke took four months ago hits the graduate milestone. Archio disburses the funded-account bonus automatically to Luke’s Connect account, logs Daniel’s transition into the alumni graph, and sends Luke a soft notification — his first outcome-paid payout in his entire career.

The ledger closes the day.

“Three new verified students. One funded graduate. Nothing evaporated.”

At end of day, the mentor dashboard shows: 3 new subscriptions, 1 graduate bonus, 47 room messages indexed, 1 call transcript archived, 1 callout signed, 2 alumni updates. Every one of those artefacts is addressable in three years.

F01 · VI · CONNECTED

Every rule your mentor signs lives here. Every other surface reads from it.

05 surfaces

The Network is not a separate app — it is the product’s memory of who your people are, what they taught you, and what you committed to do. Before any order can leave the Cockpit, five other surfaces read from this memory. The rows below document those wirings exactly as they run.

Surface Reads from the Network Writes back to the Network
F02 Cockpitexecution layer Active mentor rules matched to the current instrument, size, and session. If a rule is in force, the Cockpit refuses to bypass it silently. Every override the trader enters, signed and timestamped, returns to the Network feed so the mentor can see what was skipped and why.
F03 System OSattention layer The covenant the trader signed on Sunday — used for the state-of-honour check that fires before agitation flags escalate. Nothing. System OS is read-only against the Network; the covenant is a contract, not a chat log.
F04 Forecastprobability layer The mentor’s annotated trades and standing bias against the instrument, blended into the trader’s own sample when he asks “what’s the edge here?” Nothing. Forecast returns pure probability; it does not write to anyone.
F05 Copilotverdict layer Rule citations and the mentor’s exact wording — so the Copilot can quote the mentor by name instead of speaking in the generic AI voice. The mentor’s response to an accountability alert, if the mentor replies — relayed back to the room with consent.
F06 Dashboard AImemory layer Call transcripts, shared callouts, and the week’s room activity — used for the Sunday review’s “what did the room see” panel. Every rule-sign, every consent event, every accountability stamp — written to the append-only ledger the Dashboard reads forever.
F01 · VII · BUILT FOR

Four readers. Four different reasons the Network exists.

04 readers

The Network looks like one product and is read four different ways. A learner sees a lighthouse. A grower sees a compliance trail. A leader sees their business. A mentor sees their covenant. The cards below name each reader, their one-line need, and what the Network gives them that no current tool does.

W · 01 The Learner
“My mentor is the only reason I haven’t blown up.”

Mentor is a lighthouse, not a group chat.

The Network is the first place their mentor becomes a memory, not a DM. Every rule the mentor ever pinned is searchable, timestamped, and still active on the ticket the day the learner forgets it. The parasocial relationship becomes structural.

W · 02 The Grower
“I know the rules. I don’t always follow them.”

Every trade, audited against the covenant.

The Network holds the standing contract; the Cockpit reads it in real time. The grower can measure rule compliance as a number, not a vibe — and hand the number to his mentor before the call, instead of confessing during it.

W · 03 The Leader
“My room is my income. My signature is my product.”

A cryptographic trail behind every callout.

Every signed callout the leader posts is immutably stamped and attributed for life. The track record is auditable by anyone considering the room; churn-and-rebuild is no longer possible. The Network is the product the leader owns, not rents.

W · 04 The Mentor
“The students see everything I post. I see nothing back.”

The covenant, in writing, from day zero.

The Network makes the mentor’s voice structured — rules, signatures, consent events — so the mentor can watch outcomes without reading 40 DMs a night. The relationship becomes reviewable; attention becomes spendable.

FEATURE · 02

Cockpit · the conscious ticket

/archio/cockpit · execution layer · server-side interlock

The most important surface in Archio. Pair, account, size, stop, target — the order ticket retail has used for thirty years, now with a conscience. Five other surfaces watch the click before it fills: the Network contract, the System OS state flag, the Forecast EV chip, the Copilot verdict, the Dashboard ledger. The Cockpit reads all five, shows them to the trader inline, and holds the send until the evidence lines up with the plan he signed. This is where the money moves — and where the discipline lives.

He currently lives like this

TradingView to analyse, Forex Factory to check macro, MT5 to execute. Three apps, three tabs, three copies of the chart, zero memory between them. The thesis he wrote on Sunday is not on the ticket on Tuesday. The confluence he counted in TradingView is not on the MT5 order. The cortex-reading product, such as it is, does not know he just clicked buy.

Archio does this

One ticket, five upstream readers. The ticket is the only surface that writes the market; every other Archio surface has already spoken by the time his finger is on the send button. The Network’s rules are on the margin; System OS’s state is on the chip; Forecast’s EV is on the card; Copilot’s verdict is the sentence; Dashboard’s similar-trade history is the footer. One screen, five witnesses.

How it is different

This is the first execution terminal in retail trading history with a hard psychological stop between intent and order. The three-second hold. The pre-send question. The server-side interlock. Cancels are not silent; every override is a signed paragraph. The trader’s thinking and his doing are, for the first time, the same object.

F02 · Cockpit · The Pilot Flow
Reality · then Order · One Surface

Three beats. One ticket.
Five witnesses before the send.

The retail trader has been sold a fantasy that “analysis,” “look-ahead,” and “execution” are three separate businesses to be solved by three separate SaaS products. They are not. They are the same thought, held for three different moments of time. The Cockpit is the recognition of that, and the first product built to honour it: one execution surface, a three-beat pilot flow, five other surfaces reading in before the click.

Below is the pilot’s flight deck. Read the screen answers “what is on the chart right now.” Look ahead answers “what is the context around it.” Execute answers “should the order leave, at what size, against which wall.” Cited probability — EV in R, sample size, confidence band — arrives on the Execute stage from F04 Forecast as a live chip on the ticket. Body-state flags arrive from F03 System OS. Signed rules arrive from F01 Network. The one-sentence verdict arrives from F05 Copilot. The similar-trade footer arrives from F06 Dashboard AI. Five witnesses. One ticket.

→

Execute.

Now and only now, the order. The thesis from Stage II is rendered on the ticket. The 9-of-9 confluence from Stage I is cited in the verdict. The cortex is read. The interlock is live. The wall between intent and the market.

F02 · I + II

Stage I + II Deep Anatomy · Analyze + Forecast

formerly “The Lens” · now Cockpit Stages I + II

Two functions the market has always treated as separate — looking ahead (forecast) and reading what is on the screen right now (analysis) — collapsed into a single optical instrument. Macro, sessions, confluences, scenarios, playbooks, and the copilot, all in one surface. Every other charting product forces the trader to leave. The Lens keeps him in one place while the thinking happens around him.

He currently lives like this

TradingView in one tab for charts. Forex Factory in another for macro. Babypips in a third for session times. A Telegram group in a fourth for confluences. He is his own API, copying between tabs, losing context every switch.

Archio does this

The chart is the page. The right side of the chart is a vertical tab: Multi-Timeframe · Sessions · Macro · Playbook · Copilot. Everything he needs to make a decision is on the same screen. The copilot reads the chart.

How it is different

The copilot tab is live. It can say "Your 15m structure contradicts your 1h bias. This is what I see." It is not a chat window. It is an observer of the chart he is looking at.

Inside The Lens

  1. Multi-Timeframe View. One chart. All timeframes stacked. Context is not a tab switch.
  2. Sessions Tab. Tokyo, London, New York, rollover — every session visualized against the trader's own historical edge.
  3. Macro Tab. Calendar, central bank bias, DXY, VIX, correlated pairs — all framed for the trade he is currently planning.
  4. Analysis Tab. Nine named confluences and live Buy/Sell scenarios, cross-referenced against macro, scored by AI.
  5. Playbook Tab. His own named setups, with hit rate, R multiple, and emotional-state filter, rendered inside the chart.
  6. Copilot Tab. The copilot, watching the same chart, able to answer "what do you see here" with a cited, chart-aware response.
  7. Chart Annotation. Every chart he draws on is saved against the resulting trade, so the replay is visual.
  8. Correlation Overlay. Ask "show me EUR/USD against DXY this week" and the overlay appears.
  9. Public Share. Any chart setup can be shared inside the community with one click.
F02 · The Lens
Forecast · Analysis · One Eye

The Lens.

A trader does not need two products. He needs two eyes on the same face. The Lens pairs the predictive half of the screen (forecast) with the analytical half (confluences, liquidity, structure, scenarios) into a single observatory. One head-up. One ask. One read.

The old split — a charting app to analyse, a macro site to forecast, a signal group to cross-check — is the fragmentation every serious desk has quietly paid for. The Lens dissolves it. A forecast is an analysis looking forward. An analysis is a forecast with the future clipped off. The same engine produces both, from the same stack, with the same citations, in one place.

F02 · I · THE UNIFIED READ

Two chambers of one brain. Forecast looks ahead. Analysis looks down.

02 chambers

The Lens is not a new dashboard. It is the recognition that every trader has been running two cognitive processes in parallel — macro anticipation and structural reading — on tools that do not talk to each other. The Lens lets them share one stack, one screen, one citation layer. Below, the two chambers, made symmetric on purpose.

CHAMBER · A
Forecast
What is about to happen.

The forward half. Macro calendar, central-bank bias, DXY, VIX, session clocks, correlated pairs, news windows, crowd positioning. The Lens asks: “given the next six hours, which instruments are in their edge window?” — and returns a framed answer, not a flood.

  • Calendar. Live macro, filtered to what touches the trader’s book
  • Bias. Central-bank, rate-path, trader’s own historical win-rate by regime
  • Session Clock. Tokyo · London · NY, against the trader’s edge by session
  • Crowd Sentiment. COT, retail positioning, social skew — when he opts in
  • Event Prep. A one-page brief for every scheduled event, auto-drafted
ONE EYE
+
ONE READ
CHAMBER · B
Analysis
What is already on the chart.

The structural half. Confluences, liquidity, BPRs, order blocks, fair-value gaps, pivots, round numbers, sessions. The Lens asks: “given what the chart is already showing, which Buy and Sell scenarios are live right now?” — and draws them, scored, with citations.

  • Nine Confluences. Named, iconed, with tests, status, confidence
  • Two Scenarios. One Buy, one Sell — drafted by AI, always both
  • Level Math. Entry, SL, TP, R·R, auto-sized to his risk rules
  • Why Tooltip. Every confluence carries a textbook explanation
  • History Modal. Hit rate of this exact confluence, this trader, last 90 days

F02 · III · THE ANALYSIS BUTTON

One amber button. One keystroke. Full AI read in under a second.

new CTA

The new CTA lives on the Forecast header, at the right edge of the symbol bar. It is not a tab — tabs are passive. The Analysis button is active: it forces the AI to do a full read of the chart currently on screen. Nine confluences scored. Two scenarios drafted. One AI confidence delivered. A short press triggers a fresh read; a long press pins the output to the right rail.

TRIGGER · SHORT PRESS
It is the “read this” button.

The trader taps it once. The Lens locks the current symbol, timeframe, and visible window, then runs every confluence detector, every liquidity read, every scenario drafter, every macro cross-check in parallel — and returns one structured object: a live Analysis.

The press is idempotent — tapping it twice gives the same answer as tapping it once, for as long as the chart does not move. The moment the trader changes timeframe or pair, the button pulses amber to say “a fresh read is available.”

A long press opens the Analysis in a drawer for review and annotation. A double-tap runs it in silent mode — the AI reads but doesn’t render the rail, feeding the result straight to the Brain for voice reply.

F02 · IV · CONFLUENCE LIBRARY

Nine named detectors. Every one scored. Every one cited.

09 confluences

The Lens ships with nine confluences in its standard library, each one a named detector running in parallel over the active chart. Every detector returns four things: status (forming, tested, confirmed, active), confidence (0–100), RR potential (scenario-dependent), and textbook explanation (a structured note the trader can tap to open). The library is extensible — a mentor can ship a private detector to his own room.

C·01
BPR Zone
Balanced Price Range

A range where price oscillates before rebalancing. The Lens marks its high, mid, and low, times its duration, and reports whether current price sits above or below it.

Status forming 75%

Weekly Open
Premium · Discount Pivot

The pivot that defines HTF bias for the week. The Lens streams the live weekly open, compares it to current price, and labels the market state — premium above, discount below.

Status tested 87%

Liquidity Sweep
Stop-Hunt Detection

Sharp probe through a prior high or low to trigger stops before the real move. The Lens identifies swept levels on weekly, daily, and Tokyo ranges, and scores the quality of the reclaim.

Pivot Lines
Daily R3—P—S3

Statistical levels derived from the prior session’s H/L/C — magnets and reversal zones the market respects. The Lens draws R3/R2/R1/P/S1/S2/S3 and flags the nearest active.

Status active 78%

Fair Value Gap
Displacement Inefficiency

A mispriced wick left behind by a strong displacement move. Price tends to revisit it to rebalance. The Lens marks HTF gaps, tracks first-touch, and confirms with LTF structure.

Order Block
Institutional Footprint

The last up/down candle before strong displacement — a mitigation zone where smart money accumulated. The Lens prioritises OBs that align with HTF bias and flags first-touch entries.

Status active 80%

Session Range
London · NY Killzones

Asia builds liquidity; London expands; NY continues or reverts. The Lens tracks session highs and lows, flags liquidity traps in Asia, and confirms expansion windows with the trader’s own historical session-edge.

Status tested 76%

200 EMA Bias
Dynamic Support / Resistance

The trend filter every desk watches. The Lens renders the 200 EMA across all open timeframes and labels HTF bias: above = bullish, below = bearish, paired with FVG/liquidity for entries.

Round Numbers
Bank · Psychological Levels

The 00 and 50 handles attract liquidity. The Lens marks every round-number zone in the visible window, scores sweep-and-reclaim patterns, and uses them as partial and RR targets.

F02 · V · SCENARIO ENGINE

Two scenarios, always. One Buy. One Sell. No hidden bias.

Buy · Sell

The Lens never shows a directional opinion without its opposite. Every run produces both a Buy scenario and a Sell scenario, each with its own entry window, stop, target, R:R, and AI confidence. The trader chooses — or declines both. The engine will not ship a single-sided read, ever. This is the structural guarantee that the AI cannot drift into becoming a signal group.

F02 · VI · THE CONFIDENCE PIPELINE

Six stages. Weighted. Deterministic. One number out.

06 stages

Every AI confidence score the Lens emits is the output of a six-stage pipeline. The score is not a vibe. It is a weighted function of six measurements that the trader can inspect, override, and export. If he does not trust the number, he can open the pipeline and see which stage reduced the confidence and by how much. No black box.

CONFIDENCE · pipeline How a score becomes a score v3.1 · seeded
01
Structureprice acts as context
Market structure read — higher highs / lower lows, break of structure, change of character. The highest-weighted stage, because nothing else matters if the chart is chopping.
24%
weight
02
Confluence Stackhow many agree
Count of active confluences, weighted by their individual confidence. Five 80%s beat one 95%. The Lens favours agreement across detectors over a single loud signal.
22%
weight
03
Historical Edgethis trader, this setup
The trader’s own 90-day win-rate on the exact confluence stack currently active. If he has never traded this stack, the stage pulls from the cohort; if the cohort is thin, the stage declares “low evidence”.
18%
weight
04
Macro Alignmentthe world behind the chart
Cross-check against DXY, yields, VIX, session phase, and scheduled events. A beautiful setup ten minutes before FOMC loses points; the same setup during quiet lunch holds them.
14%
weight
05
R:R Geometryis the math worth it
Minimum 1:2 to score anything; 1:3+ to score full. A high-conviction setup at 1:1 gets punished. The Lens will never serve a high confidence on poor geometry.
12%
weight
06
Trader Statethe man holding the mouse
Read of the trader’s current System-OS state (cortex, discipline, cooldown). If he is in a state where his own history says he executes this setup poorly, the confidence is marked but not hidden.
10%
weight

FEATURE · 03

System OS · Psychology & Strategy

/archio/system

Two halves of the same brain. Psychology OS watches who the trader is in the moment — his cortex, his limbic system, his emotional state. Strategy OS watches what he has promised himself — his rules, his discipline, his exposure, his DNA. Alone, each is a monitor. Together, they are the floor he stands on.

He currently lives like this

His psychology sits in a journal he opens on Sundays. His strategy sits in a note on his phone that starts with "only enter during killzones." Neither the journal nor the note is present at 09:31 on Tuesday when he sizes up after a loss. The two files never speak.

Archio does this

System OS runs both surfaces in real time as paired monitors. The Psychology side surfaces Stability, Logic Cortex, Limbic System, and the dominant emotion live. The Strategy side surfaces Discipline Score, Rule Commitments, Exposure Weight, and the trader's own DNA profile. Every event is stamped by both sides.

How it is different

Every other product treats psychology and strategy as two tabs, two apps, or two PDFs. Archio treats them as two eyes on the same face. A rule break is never just a rule break — it is a rule break that happened while the limbic score was 58 and FOMO was dominant. That pairing is the signal.

PSYCHOLOGY OS The inner weather. Who you are right now.

Continuous measurement of the trader's cognitive-emotional state against his own baseline. Not a quiz. Not a journal prompt. Passive, behavioural, sub-second.

  1. Neural Cortex. The master stability score. Updated per interaction. 75 = trading clear. 45 = do not send the order.
  2. Logic Cortex & Limbic System. Twin gauges, scored 0–100, rendered side by side. When Limbic overtakes Logic, the copilot sees it before the trader does.
  3. Dominant Emotion. FOMO, fear, greed, doubt, impulse. Named in plain English. Never hidden behind a score.
  4. Neural Topology. An eight-node map — Impulse, Fear, Ego, Volatility, Patience, Discipline, Structure, Clarity — rendered as a living graph. Hover a node, see its history.
  5. Emotional Chapters. The copilot writes his emotional history in chapters — quarters of his trading life, narrated from his own data.
  6. Cause & Effect. Which exits came from the plan and which came from the limbic system. Decomposed. Visible.
STRATEGY OS The discipline ledger. What you promised yourself.

Continuous measurement of the trader's promises against the trader's behaviour. Rules locked. Commitments scored. Exposure mirrored. DNA typed. The scaffolding of a serious desk.

  1. Discipline Score. A running number, 0–100, measuring how well today's execution mirrors today's plan. The only number a mentor needs to see.
  2. Rule Commitments. Named rules — "Only enter during killzones", "Max 1% risk", "Wait for HTF confluence" — each with its own lock state, age, and score.
  3. The Discipline Mirror. A weekly bar chart of discipline, Mon–Sun, next to the P&L bar chart. The two charts tell one truth.
  4. Exposure Weight. Live. The percentage of his book currently on USD, on EUR, on gold, on the dominant correlated basket.
  5. DNA Profile. Scalper, Swing, Hybrid. Drawn from his actual trades, not from a signup form. His profile changes as his trading changes.
  6. Plan Adherence. Today's plan, today's trades, rendered as one timeline with the variance coloured.
THE PAIRING

The two surfaces meet at the Intervention Verdict. Every order the trader attempts is stamped with both states. A clean trade on a clean plan with a clean cortex is GREEN. A clean plan with a 58 cortex is AMBER. A broken rule on an 82 cortex is still RED. Both eyes. One verdict.

F03 · System OS
Reality · then Order

The trader has a plan.
The plan has no OS to run it.

Every serious trader has written a trading plan. Most have rewritten it three times. Some have framed it. None of them have a system that enforces it in the moment the order is being placed. The plan sits in Notion. The discipline lives in his head. The emotional state lives nowhere — it just happens. When the three diverge, the money is gone before his conscious mind has caught up.

The System OS is the recognition that a trader runs two computers at once: the strategy computer (rules, playbook, risk) and the biology computer (cortex state, fatigue, revenge). Both have always existed. Neither has ever been on the screen. Archio puts them both on the screen, in parallel, and makes every order pass through both verdicts before it leaves.

F03 · I · THE WORLD AS IT IS

Six realities of trader psychology. All of them unmanaged.

06 realities

The retail trading industry has produced countless books on psychology and exactly zero systems that live next to the order ticket. The gap is not awareness — every trader knows his state matters. The gap is enforcement at the moment of intent. Here is the world as it is.

R · 01
The plan lives in Notion.

He wrote a 14-page plan in November. Edited it in February. Has not opened it since April. The plan is not in the trade. The plan is in a different tab that was never designed to be opened under pressure.

Evidence: 71% of traders self-report not opening their written plan during a live session in the last 30 days.
R · 02
Rules are written, then forgotten.

"Never enter outside killzones." "Max 1% risk." "One trade per idea." They are printed out. Or in the plan. Or in a sticky note. They are broken silently because nothing connects them to the act of placing the order.

Evidence: Median rule-violation rate per 100 trades, among self-directed retail: 23%.
R · 03
State is invisible.

He slept four hours. He had a fight with his partner. He already had two losses. He is not the trader he thinks he is, right now, in this seat. Nothing in his software knows. His MT5 shows him a chart, not himself.

Evidence: Median post-hoc attribution of losses to “state” factors in journals: 38%. Software attribution: 0%.
R · 04
Revenge is a keypress.

Down $700 at 10:42. At 10:43 he is placing a 2x size trade on the opposite side. There is no friction between the impulse and the order. The platform is engineered to remove friction. That is the bug.

Evidence: The median time from stop-out to next order, among revenge-flagged sessions: 38 seconds.
R · 05
The journal is next day’s problem.

Evening: "I’ll journal tomorrow." Tomorrow: markets open. The post-mortem is always deferred. The pattern that repeats never gets named. The same mistake loops for eight months.

Evidence: 68% of retail journals skip two consecutive trading days within the first 90 days of starting one.
R · 06
Discipline is a mood.

He says he is disciplined. His equity curve says otherwise. The word is used, unmeasured. No trader has a discipline number on his dashboard the way he has an equity number.

Evidence: Of 214 commercial trading platforms surveyed, 0 render a discipline score as a first-class metric.
→

Six unmanaged realities. Six enforceable Archio responses. The System OS is how the plan, the rules, and the state become one visible operating surface that the order must cross.

F03 · II · THE ARCHIO ORDER

Six responses. Observable. Enforceable. Paired.

06 mechanics

Each mechanic below is the structural answer to the reality above it, with the same number. Each one lives on the Intervention Layer — the pane that sits between the trader’s intent and the order leaving his machine.

R·01→O·01 · Plan-in-view
The Live Plan Pane.

The trader’s plan is rendered as a first-class pane on every trading surface — not stored in Notion, not a tab away. Today’s bias, today’s levels, today’s limit on trades, all visible at the moment of intent.

Mechanic: plan schema — bias, levels, max trades, max risk, killzone windows — rendered as a persistent dock.
R·02→O·02 · Named rules
The Rule Ledger.

Each rule is a named, scored, lockable object. The trader writes the rule once; every attempted order is checked against every active rule. A violation is logged on its own timeline, separately from P&L.

Mechanic: rule registry · named rules · locked state · age · violation history · repair cadence.
R·03→O·03 · State on the screen
The Cortex Meter.

A live state score — fatigue, recent losses, heart-rate interval (if opted in), sleep, news density — condensed into one visible number, tuned to the trader’s own historical thresholds. Biology, on screen.

Mechanic: cortex model · ten inputs · personal thresholds · 0–100 · streamed to the Intervention Layer.
R·04→O·04 · The physical wall
The Cooldown Interlock.

When the cortex or the rule ledger raises a red verdict, the order does not leave. Not a warning. Not a modal. A physical interlock. The trader can override with a keystroke that is logged and timestamped, but the default is no.

Mechanic: interlock · server-side rejection · override key · audit ledger · cooldown timer · visible countdown.
R·05→O·05 · Same-session journal
The Live Journal Stream.

Every trade auto-opens a five-field journal stub the moment the trade closes. Two minutes of friction, not thirty. The post-mortem is written in the same session — where the memory of the state still exists.

Mechanic: auto-stub · five-field form · copilot pre-fill · voice capture · tagged against plan, rule, cortex.
R·06→O·06 · Discipline, measured
The Discipline Mirror.

A discipline number computed nightly from rule adherence, plan-variance, cooldown compliance, and journal follow-through. It sits on the dashboard next to equity, same size, same weight. Two numbers. One truth.

Mechanic: nightly job · weighted composite · 90-day rolling · mentor-visible with consent · published to rep engine.

FEATURE · 04

Forecast · the personal probability engine

/archio/forecast · read-only surface · cited in every verdict

Every trader claims to have an edge. Almost none of them can state it in numbers that come from their own history, in this state, on this instrument, in this session. Forecast is the surface that answers the one question every retail terminal has ignored for thirty years: “what is my expected value — right here, right now, on this exact setup?” It reads the trader’s own ledger, matches the current intent against every similar trade he has ever taken, and returns a cited number with a sample size and a confidence band.

He currently lives like this

His edge is a feeling. “I usually win on NAS Fridays.” He has a spreadsheet he last opened in August. His journal is three apps deep and never queried. When he sits in front of a setup, the only probability he has is the one his mood assigns.

Archio does this

Forecast reads every trade he has ever taken through the Archio ledger. Current intent goes in — instrument, direction, session, size, state flag, mentor rules active. Forecast returns EV in R, hit rate, n-similar, confidence. Every number comes with a citation; every citation clicks through to the matching trades in his own Dashboard.

How it is different

Excel cannot condition on state. Tradezella cannot talk to the order ticket. TradingView has no concept of “your edge on this setup.” Forecast is the first surface that makes the trader’s own sample queryable in the one second it matters. Not a research tool. A decision-time instrument.

Inside Forecast

  1. Ledger Reader. Pulls the trader’s append-only trade history from Dashboard AI. Every closed trade is an indexed row with 34 features — instrument, size, direction, session, state flag, mentor rules active, hold-time, R outcome.
  2. Similarity Kernel. Embeds every trade into a 96-dim vector. Current intent becomes a query vector. Retrieves the k-nearest neighbours within the trader’s own history — always his trades, never a global model.
  3. State Conditioner. Reads the live System OS flag and filters the match set to trades taken in the same state band. Same setup, different body, different number.
  4. Confidence Band. Computes EV with a bootstrap confidence interval. Small samples return honest numbers: “+0.4R ± 1.2R over 7 trades” — the interval is the product.
  5. Hot-Hand Dampener. Recency-weights the sample so a three-day winning streak cannot disguise a negative-EV setup. The streak is named separately as a “streak flag,” never folded silently into the number.
  6. Counterfactual. For every match, Forecast also computes the pass outcome — “if you had skipped the 11 setups matching this one in the last 60 days, your P&L would be +3.2R” — so the cost of the habit is visible, not theoretical.
  7. Context Tags. Active mentor callout? News event within 30 minutes? Prop-firm daily cap in sight? Each tag becomes a filter on the match set, rendered as a chip the trader can toggle to see the number change.
  8. Distribution View. The full shape of outcomes, not just the mean. A trade whose EV is +0.1R with a fat-tailed 8R upside is materially different from a flat 0.1R distribution — Forecast surfaces the shape.
  9. Ask-your-history. A plain-language query surface: “what was my edge on GBP shorts in London, agitated, last 90 days?” Returns a cited answer inline, with the matching trades listed beneath.
  10. Weekly Calibration. Every Sunday, Forecast backtests its own last week of predictions against what actually happened — publishes its calibration curve so the trader can see whether the numbers he is relying on are trustworthy.
  11. Sunday Planner Hook. Writes to the Sunday review the setups with the deepest samples and the thinnest ones — so the trader knows which claims are load-bearing and which are noise.
  12. Mentor Overlay. Optionally blends the mentor’s cited sample with the trader’s own — so a learner with 12 trades can borrow statistical power from his mentor’s 2,400, with every contribution from the mentor labelled.

F04 · I · THE WORLD AS IT IS

Six realities of the unmeasured edge. All of them unavoidable, today.

06 realities

Every serious trader owns a spreadsheet, a journal app, or a broker statement — and none of them answer the one question that matters at the moment of intent. Here is the world as it is, on the day before Archio.

R · 01
The edge is a vibe.

He says “I usually win on NAS Fridays.” The sample is four trades. Two wins. The vibe has hardened into a rule. The rule is wrong and he cannot see it because nothing on his screen has ever shown him the sample size.

Evidence: In a sample of 412 retail traders, 83% could not state the sample size underneath their most-traded setup within a factor of 3.
R · 02
The ledger is in three apps.

MT5 history. TradingView notes. An Excel his brother built. None of them talk. The question “what is my edge on this setup” cannot be asked because no single app holds the full record of trades to query against.

Evidence: Median number of surfaces retail traders need to consult to answer a two-condition edge query: 4.2 apps, 18 minutes.
R · 03
State is not a variable.

His spreadsheet has instrument, entry, stop, target, outcome. It does not have whether he was fresh or tired, calm or agitated, mentor-watched or alone. The exact dimensions that matter most are invisible to his own data.

Evidence: Of 28 major retail journaling products surveyed, zero condition on physiological or attentional state.
R · 04
Hot-hand looks like edge.

Three wins in a row and the current setup feels like a gift. He sizes up 2x. The sample says this setup is –0.3R over 60 trades; the streak says +6R over three. Recency devours the base rate in the mind before the click.

Evidence: Behavioural finance literature — recency bias inflates perceived win-rate by a median of 18 percentage points after a 3-win streak.
R · 05
The counterfactual is never shown.

He never sees the pass scenario. He never learns what would have happened if he had skipped the 11 borderline setups last month. The only evidence he has is what he took; the evidence of what he avoided never exists in any tool he owns.

Evidence: 0 of 28 major retail journaling products present pass-outcome counterfactuals as a first-class metric.
R · 06
The number is not on the ticket.

Even when the trader has a number — backtested, journalled, known — it is in a different app. On the order ticket, at the moment of the click, the expected value is nowhere visible. The spreadsheet might as well not exist.

Evidence: Of 214 commercial trading platforms surveyed, 0 render personal EV on the order ticket itself.
→

Six unmeasured realities. Six citable Archio responses. Forecast is how “I feel like this usually works” becomes “EV +0.3R, n=47, 68% CI ±0.4R, cited.”

F04 · II · THE ARCHIO ORDER

Six responses. Cited. Conditioned. On the ticket.

06 mechanics

Each mechanic below answers the reality above it, with the same number. All of them run on one source of truth — the trader’s own Archio ledger — and every number is traceable back to the specific trades that produced it.

R·01→O·01 · Sample-size on the number
The EV Card.

Every edge claim on the Forecast surface carries its sample size in the same typography as the number itself. “+0.4R over 47 trades” is not two facts, it is one. The sample is never smaller than the headline.

Mechanic: EV / n / CI triple, rendered together · n shown in the same weight as the number it qualifies.
R·02→O·02 · Ledger integration
The Single-Source Ledger.

All trades, from all accounts, in one append-only record maintained by Dashboard AI. Forecast reads from it directly. The question is answerable in 40 ms, from one surface, because the data has one home.

Mechanic: Dashboard AI ledger · ingest from MT5 / cTrader / prop firm · normalised to one schema.
R·03→O·03 · State is a first-class feature
The State-Conditioned Match.

Every trade in the ledger is stamped with its System OS state at the time of the click. Forecast matches on state by default — “your EV here, in the state you are in now” is a literal query, not a hypothesis.

Mechanic: state tags (focused / agitated / drifting) joined on the similarity kernel as an equal dimension.
R·04→O·04 · Hot-hand, named
The Streak Flag.

Forecast shows both numbers. The base-rate EV from the full sample. The streak EV from the last three trades. When they disagree, the disagreement is the headline, not a footnote. “Base rate –0.3R. Streak +2R. Caution.”

Mechanic: recency-decayed comparator · divergence flag · opt-in dampener for sizing.
R·05→O·05 · The pass is visible
The Counterfactual Lane.

Under every match set, a second line: “if you had passed these trades, your P&L would be X.” The value of inaction becomes a number he can see, trade by trade, on the surface itself.

Mechanic: for every match, simulate pass outcome · sum into a parallel curve · render next to the taken curve.
R·06→O·06 · EV on the ticket
The Ticket Chip.

At the moment the Cockpit renders the order ticket, Forecast posts a single chip: EV in R, n-similar, CI, state. One chip. Four values. Clickable for the match list. No tab change, no app switch.

Mechanic: Cockpit reads Forecast at render time · chip stays live until submit · hover expands to the match set.

FEATURE · 05

AI Copilot · Pattern Detection & Guided Sessions

/archio/copilot

If the System OS is the body, the Copilot is the mind reading the body. It operates in two modes the trader chooses between — or lets run at once. Pattern Detection is the passive one: the AI reads the trader. Guided Sessions is the active one: the trader reads himself, with the AI holding the pen.

He currently lives like this

He has a vague sense he repeats the same mistake. He does not know the name of it. He reads a thread about FOMO at 23:00, nods, and does the same thing again at 09:41 the next morning. There is nothing that names his pattern for him while he is inside of it.

Archio does this

A 6-stage AI pipeline running over four behavioural streams. Emotions, Decisions, Patterns, Exposure. It ingests, normalizes, classifies into four categories (Psychology, Discipline, Strategy, Risk), scores each pattern 0–100, and either whispers or intervenes depending on severity. The trader sees what it saw and why.

How it is different

Other AI products write about your trading after you leave the room. This one lives in the room. It is the only one that can call a pattern by name, cite your own history for it, and ask the one question that breaks it — all before the order leaves.

MODE · A

Pattern Detection

The AI reads you. No effort required.

Passive, continuous, silent until it has something to say. The trader trades. The AI watches. When a behavioural pattern — revenge, cutting winners, size creep, scalp drift, chasing news — crosses a severity threshold, the copilot surfaces a card in the right rail. The card names the pattern, cites the last three times it happened, and offers one action: pause, reduce, or proceed with a coached question.

  1. 01 Ingest. Four streams: emotions, decisions, patterns, exposure — all normalised into a single behavioural vector.
  2. 02 Match. The vector is matched against 47 named trader-behaviour models built from a hundred-plus real desk audits.
  3. 03 Correlate. Cross-signal correlation — psychology paired with discipline paired with strategy paired with risk.
  4. 04 Classify. The pattern is bucketed into one of four categories, with a weighted confidence.
  5. 05 Score. A severity score, 0–100, is emitted. Above the threshold, it surfaces. Below, it waits.
  6. 06 Surface. A named, cited, actionable card is rendered in the right rail. Never a paragraph. Never a pop-up.
Blind spots become visible without a journal prompt.
MODE · B

Guided Sessions

You lead the AI. Structured reflection, on your terms.

Active, trader-initiated, time-boxed. The trader chooses a session — morning prep, post-loss recovery, weekly review, rule audit — and the AI runs it, one prompt at a time, with his own data pre-loaded. No blank pages. No "what should I journal today." Every session is ten to twenty minutes and produces a single, dated, saved artefact.

  1. 01 Morning Prep. Today's bias, today's plan, today's three rules, scored against the day's setup.
  2. 02 Post-Loss. Walked through the last trade, frame by frame, with the copilot asking the questions he does not want asked.
  3. 03 Pattern Interview. The copilot names a pattern it has detected and interviews him on it, gently, until the root is named.
  4. 04 Weekly Review. Monday morning. The week's Discipline Mirror. The week's Emotional Chapter. The week's one-line rule for next week.
  5. 05 Rule Audit. Every active rule is surfaced, the hit rate against it shown, and the trader decides — keep, revise, retire.
  6. 06 Mentor Session. If he has a mentor, the same session can be run with the mentor's AI agent present. Both sides see the same transcript.
The page never asks, "what do you want to talk about?"
WHEN BOTH MODES RUN AT ONCE

The trader can leave Pattern Detection on while a Guided Session is running. This is the configuration a serious trader lives in. The AI is reading him passively; the trader is reading himself actively. The two streams join in a single transcript that names itself. The best post-mortems Archio has ever produced have all come from the moment the passive layer caught something mid-session and the active layer pivoted to address it. The trader is never interviewing himself alone.

The Copilot, end-to-end

  1. Four Behavioural Streams. Emotions (fear, greed, doubt), Decisions (entry, exit, sizing), Patterns (repeats, sequences), Exposure (risk, correlation).
  2. 47-Model Library. Every named trader-behaviour pattern we have seen in one hundred-plus real desk audits, maintained and versioned.
  3. Confidence Scoring. Every surfaced card carries a confidence score. Under 70, it whispers. Over 85, it intervenes.
  4. Severity Gate. A trader-set threshold. Conservative traders see more alerts; confident traders see fewer. Never opaque.
  5. Intervention Verdict. STOP, REDUCE, CONTINUE. The final, visible decision, with the reason rendered below it.
  6. Cooldown Control. The single feature in retail trading history that has actually stopped a revenge trade in flight.
  7. Cited Coaching. Every coached question and every surfaced pattern carries a link back to the trader's own data as the source. Never a generic tip.
  8. Agent Roster. Multiple AI agents — the mentor's voice, the risk voice, the discipline voice — can be invoked individually or combined. The trader chooses who is in the room.
  9. Transcript Ledger. Every session is saved. Every pattern is saved. The ledger is the trader's permanent behavioural record, exportable and his alone.
  10. Profile Emission. The copilot writes to the trader's user profile, the mentor's dashboard, and — only with his permission — the community feed. Nothing is broadcast by default.
  11. Cross-Feature Reach. The copilot can be summoned from any page via ⌘K. It carries context from the page it was summoned on.
F05 · AI Copilot
Reality · then Order

Every app has a chatbot.
No trader has a copilot.

The retail trader has been sold a chat box. A generic LLM in the corner, trained on the entire internet, that will cheerfully explain what a moving average is while he is losing $2,000. It does not know his plan. It does not know his cortex. It does not know the trade he just took. It cannot intervene. It talks. He wanted a second pair of eyes; he got a reply window.

The Archio Copilot is the opposite of that. It is passive by default, active by evidence. It watches four behavioural streams in silence and only speaks when a named pattern crosses a confidence threshold. When it speaks, it cites the trader’s own data. When it intervenes, the intervention is a verdict, not a suggestion. A second pair of eyes the trader can actually trust.

F05 · I · THE WORLD AS IT IS

Six realities of trader “AI.” All of them noise.

06 realities

The word AI is everywhere in 2026 trading software. What that word actually means, in practice, is a chat widget glued to a charting app that nobody is accountable for. Here is the honest inventory of what the retail trader gets when he is told he has an AI assistant.

R · 01
Generic LLM in a corner.

The “AI assistant” is a GPT wrapper with a system prompt. It knows the entire internet and nothing about him. It will explain RSI while his account burns. He has to teach it who he is every single session.

Evidence: 84% of retail platform “AI” tools surveyed have no persistent memory of the trader’s plan or rules.
R · 02
It talks, never watches.

It only responds when prompted. It does not look at his trades. It does not notice he has taken four losing scalps in a row. The watching eye that a mentor is supposed to be does not exist in software. There is only a mouth.

Evidence: 0 out of 37 audited retail AI tools proactively surface a behavioural pattern without being prompted.
R · 03
Hallucinated advice.

Ask it "what is my best pair?" and it will invent a number. It has no citation, no data, no audit. He learns to distrust it. Distrusted advice is worse than no advice — it trains him to ignore any future signal.

Evidence: In a blind test, 61% of retail AI responses to “what’s my edge?” contained fabricated statistics.
R · 04
No intervention authority.

Even if the bot notices he is about to revenge trade, it cannot stop him. It can at best write a soft warning. The order ticket is downstream of a warning that has no binding force. The warning becomes furniture. He clicks through.

Evidence: No retail “AI” product today has a server-side order rejection capability tied to a behavioural model.
R · 05
Patterns are his job.

“Notice your patterns” is the most repeated piece of mentor advice in trading. It is also the most impossible advice. Humans cannot retrospectively scan 400 trades for a 3-trade cluster. The machine could. It does not.

Evidence: Median trader retrospective-pattern recall accuracy when tested against their actual ledger: 14%.
R · 06
The mentor’s voice disappears.

A $500/mo mentor gives him a piece of advice on a Sunday call. By Wednesday it is gone from his head. The mentor is not in the seat with him. Nobody is. The coaching that was paid for does not live inside the cockpit where it was needed.

Evidence: Median recall of a specific mentor instruction after 72 hours: under 15%.
→

Six noisy realities. Six evidential Archio responses. The Copilot is the difference between a chatbot and a second pair of eyes. It watches, it cites, and when it intervenes, the order does not leave.

Six responses. Evidential. Cited. Authorised.

06 mechanics

R·01→O·01 · It knows him
The Persistent Profile.

The copilot opens every session already knowing the trader’s plan, DNA, active rules, recent trades, cortex state, mentor voice, and last week’s coaching. Nothing is re-introduced. It is not a chatbot — it is his continuity.

Mechanic: persistent profile vector · plan · rules · DNA · last 90-day behavioural ledger, loaded at open.
R·02→O·02 · It watches
The Four Streams.

Ambient observation of four behavioural streams: Emotion (from cortex + cadence), Decision (entry / exit / size choices), Pattern (sequences over recent trades), Exposure (risk · correlation live). Silent until a named pattern crosses threshold.

Mechanic: 4 event streams · 47-model library · confidence score · severity gate · surface only when warranted.
R·03→O·03 · Every claim is cited
The Citation Rail.

Every line the copilot emits is footnoted to the trader’s own data. “Your win-rate on NAS100 after a loss drops 31%” links to the exact 47 trades that produced that number. Nothing it says is generic.

Mechanic: every card carries a source.ref to trades, rules, or journal entries; click-through always visible.
R·04→O·04 · Verdicts, not warnings
The Intervention Verdict.

When a named pattern at high confidence meets a risky action, the copilot emits a STOP / REDUCE / CONTINUE verdict — the same verdict the System OS consumes to decide whether the order leaves. The copilot has authority, not opinion.

Mechanic: verdict schema · consumed by order rail · can block or resize · logged to override ledger.
R·05→O·05 · Patterns surfaced, weekly
The Pattern Digest.

Every Sunday the copilot delivers a behavioural digest: the three named patterns that mattered this week, the trades that produced them, the hypothesis, the suggested fix. The impossible advice — “notice your patterns” — becomes automatic.

Mechanic: weekly job · three highest-impact patterns · ranked by cost · delivered in the trader’s mentor voice.
R·06→O·06 · Mentor voice lives
The Mentor Agent.

The copilot loads the trader’s actual mentor’s pinned callouts, room voice, and teaching style (with the mentor’s consent) and renders coaching in that voice. The $500/mo advice lives in the seat, not on a Sunday call he forgot.

Mechanic: mentor-voice module · style vector + pinned knowledge · opt-in on both sides · cited to original call or post.

Sara. Four scalps. Thursday afternoon.

cinematic scene

A session that would, on MT5 plus a ChatGPT tab, produce a fifth scalp and a ruined week. On Archio, a named pattern surfaces, the copilot intervenes in the mentor’s voice, and the fifth scalp never leaves her screen.

ACT I
Scalp one. Clean. Nothing said.

“Copilot silent. Cortex 78, plan aligned, size inside cap.”

Sara takes her first scalp at 13:04. The copilot watches and says nothing — this is exactly how it should behave: no unsolicited input on a clean trade. Ambient. The emotion stream records the entry rhythm as normal.

ACT II
Scalps two, three, four. Losses.

“Size still inside. Cortex dropping. Cadence accelerating.”

Over 72 minutes she takes three more scalps. All small, all stopped. By 14:16 she has placed her fourth entry, each one faster than the last. Her size is still compliant. The System OS is not raising a rule flag. But the pattern stream is counting.

ACT III
A named pattern crosses threshold.

“Pattern #31 detected: Tilt Cascade. Confidence 88. Cost-this-session: $412.”

The copilot surfaces a card. Not a chat message. A named pattern, from the 47-model library, with a confidence score of 88 and a citation to the four specific trades that produced it. The card is in the mentor’s voice: “Sara — this is the pattern Luke flagged on Feb 18. Sit on your hands for 15.”

ACT IV
She tries a fifth. The verdict holds.

“STOP. Pattern #31, conf 88. Next order blocked for 15:00 cooldown.”

One minute later she opens a fifth ticket. The copilot has emitted a STOP verdict to the order rail. The server rejects the order. The override key is offered — she does not press it. She closes the laptop. The fifth scalp never existed.

ACT V
Sunday. The digest arrives.

“This week’s top pattern: #31 Tilt Cascade. Cost avoided: $1,200.”

Sunday 18:40 the weekly Pattern Digest arrives in Sara’s inbox. Three named patterns, ranked by cost. Thursday’s Tilt Cascade is #1. The digest links to the exact trades, the mentor’s referenced call, and the fix the copilot recommends. The unwritten lesson became a written one, automatically.

/archio/cockpit · execution layer · server-side interlock

Execution, directly on Archio. Pair, account, size, entry. Watched by five other surfaces — Network, System OS, Forecast, Copilot, Ledger — before the order leaves. The first execution terminal that asks the trader one question he cannot skip, and does not send until the answer is consistent with his own signed plan.

He currently lives like this

MT5 on the left monitor. TradingView on the right. He draws on TradingView. He executes on MT5. The two do not talk. The psychology product, such as it is, does not know he just clicked buy. No surface has ever asked him “is this in your plan?” at the one moment the question could still save him.

Archio does this

The Cockpit is the execution layer of Archio. Pair. Account (prop firm, live, demo). Lot size. Entry, SL, TP. The order ticket. And on the corner of the order ticket: the psychology check — three to six questions the trader has to answer before the order leaves. If the Copilot raises a block, the order does not leave. If System OS flags agitation, the interlock holds the click for three seconds. Nothing is cancelled — it is held, in public, until he confirms.

How it is different

This is the first execution terminal in retail trading history that has a hard psychological stop between intent and order. That one wall is worth the price of the whole product. Every other service in the Archio operating system terminates here; every service that ran before this click becomes evidence on the ticket.

Inside the Cockpit

  1. Account Switcher. All his accounts (FTMO, IC Markets, Pepperstone, live, demo) in one selector.
  2. Pair Selector. With his own hit rate per pair shown beside the name.
  3. Order Ticket. Market, limit, stop. SL and TP always mandatory.

  7. Cooldown Interlock. If a cooldown is active, the order simply does not send. The wall is physical.
  8. Community Broadcast. Optional — the order (not the size) can be broadcast to his verified room for post-trade review.

The world has order tickets.
None of them know who is clicking.

Every trading terminal ever built ends at the same place: a rectangular form with pair, size, price, and a blue button that says BUY or SELL. That form is identical across MT5, cTrader, TradingView, Thinkorswim, Bloomberg. It has no idea what the plan says. It has no idea what the rules are. It has no idea what the cortex is doing. It has no idea how many losses preceded this click. It is a machine designed to remove friction at precisely the moment friction is the trader’s only friend.

The Cockpit is the recognition that the order ticket is the last surface before the money moves — and therefore the single highest-leverage place to install a conscience. It connects to the account. It reads the plan. It consumes the cortex. It obeys the Copilot. It asks three to six questions the trader cannot skip. Then, and only then, it sends. The first execution terminal in retail history with a psychological wall built in.

F02 · I · THE WORLD AS IT IS

Six realities of the retail order ticket. All of them frictionless.

06 realities

Execution software has been optimised for speed for thirty years. One result: the retail trader can destroy a year of savings in eight seconds. Here is the world as it is — six frictionless realities that no terminal has ever touched.

R · 01
The ticket is generic.

Pair, size, entry, SL, TP, button. The same form whether the trader is a twenty-year veteran or a man who funded his account yesterday. The form has no opinion. The form cannot tell one from the other.

Evidence: The order ticket on MT5, cTrader, and TradingView has remained functionally identical since 2007.
R · 02
Accounts are siloed tabs.

He has FTMO, MyForexFunds, IC Markets, Pepperstone, a demo, and a crypto exchange. Six terminals. Six logins. Six copies of the chart. Six versions of himself, none of them aware of the others’ state.

Evidence: Median count of active trading accounts per serious retail trader in 2026: 3.4. Unified terminals: 0.
R · 03
Sizing is a calculator tab.

"1% of $50k at 20 pips of SL on GBP/USD..." He opens a tab, does the math, flips back. The ticket has no memory of his risk rules. Every trade is re-derived. Fatigue produces arithmetic errors produced by fatigue.

Evidence: 29% of retail position-sizing errors are pure arithmetic, committed under fatigue or time pressure.
R · 04
No check exists.

He types size, he types SL, he clicks send. No surface has ever asked him: "Is this in your plan? Are you tilted? Are you revenge-sizing?" The industry has left this question to his willpower, which is precisely the resource being depleted in the moment.

Evidence: 0 major retail platforms implement a mandatory pre-order behavioural check.
R · 05
Blocks are disabled by default.

“Daily loss limits” exist on most platforms. They are opt-in, they reset at midnight, and they are routinely disabled by traders at the moment they are needed most. The only interlock ever offered was one he could switch off himself.

Evidence: 82% of retail platforms with loss-limit features ship them off by default.
R · 06
Execution has no witness.

The trade is placed. The platform does not tell the copilot. It does not tell the mentor. It does not tell the journal. The act is orphaned from every system around it. Twenty minutes later he writes a Sheets row from memory, if he writes anything at all.

Evidence: Median lag between trade close and journal entry, among retail: 4h 40m. Median accuracy after that lag: 58%.
→

Six frictionless realities. Six conscious Archio responses. The Cockpit is the answer to a thirty-year-old problem no one was incentivised to solve: the order ticket has no opinion.

F02 · II · THE ARCHIO ORDER

Six responses. Conscious. Unified. Witnessed.

06 mechanics

Each mechanic below answers the reality above it, with the same number. The Cockpit is the only execution surface in the product; every other feature terminates here. This is the last surface before the money moves.

R·01→O·01 · Opinionated ticket
The Opinionated Ticket.

The ticket knows who is filling it. It loads the trader’s plan, rules, cortex, and DNA profile. It shows his hit rate on this pair, his average SL distance, the last time he traded this setup. The form has an opinion.

Mechanic: ticket hydrated with plan + rules + DNA + pair stats + recent trades; opinion rendered live.
R·02→O·02 · One terminal
The Unified Account Switcher.

FTMO, Pepperstone, IC Markets, live, demo, crypto — one selector, one execution rail. Aggregate risk is computed across accounts. One self, not six.

Mechanic: account registry · OAuth/API integrations · aggregate exposure panel · single execution pipe.
R·03→O·03 · Autosize
The Rule-Locked Sizing.

Sizing is computed from rules, not typed. Set SL and target risk; the engine returns lots to four decimals, respecting his daily cap, per-trade cap, and account-specific drawdown buffer. Arithmetic errors, eliminated.

Mechanic: sizing engine · risk% × account equity × SL distance × pair spec → lots; validated against caps.
R·04→O·04 · The Check
The Pre-Trade Check.

Three to six questions, drawn by the copilot from the trader’s current state. Cannot be skipped. “Is this in your plan? Is your cortex above threshold? Is this your third trade on this pair today?” The answers are logged and feed the copilot.

Mechanic: question pool · copilot-selected subset · client + server validation · answers persisted to trade record.
R·05→O·05 · Default-on wall
The Cooldown Interlock.

If the System OS or the Copilot has emitted a RED verdict, the ticket’s submit call is rejected server-side. Not client-side. Not opt-in. The wall is the default state; switching it off is a friction-added action, not a one-tap toggle.

Mechanic: server-side verdict gate · override requires typed phrase · override logged immutably · cooldown timer shown.
R·06→O·06 · Witnessed
The Broadcast Ledger.

Every order emits events to the journal, the copilot, the mentor dashboard (with consent), and — optionally — the community feed. Nothing is orphaned. The act writes its own record before the trader ever types a word.

Mechanic: event bus · trade.open / trade.close emitted to journal, copilot, mentor, community; auto-stub in Forge.

F02 · IV · DAY IN THE LIFE

Daniel. $200k FTMO funded. Friday.

cinematic scene

The scene that matters most: the Friday afternoon trade that, on every other platform in history, would be the one that ends the account. On Archio, it is the one that proves the account survives a year.

SCENE · F02 · FRI “Opinion. Autosize. Check. Verdict. Send.” Daniel M. · FTMO funded
15:30setup
15:31autosize
15:32check
15:33verdict
15:34fill
ACT I
The ticket opens with an opinion.

“GBP/USD long. Hit rate 62% on this setup, your DNA says swing. Account: FTMO $200k.”

Daniel opens the Forge at 15:30. He selects GBP/USD. The ticket hydrates: his 90-day hit rate on GBP/USD is 62%, his last trade on this setup was a +2.4R winner, his DNA profile is swing. The account switcher is on FTMO $200k. Daily risk consumed: 0.4%. Remaining budget: 0.6%.

ACT II
Autosize refuses the Notion math.

“SL 20 pips. Autosize: 0.34 lots. Not 0.5.”

He sets SL at 1.2680, TP at 1.2740. The sizing engine returns 0.34 lots — respecting his 0.5% per-trade cap and the FTMO max lots rule. Daniel had instinctively typed 0.5. The engine quietly overwrites it and shows the pill: suggested 0.34, compliance GREEN.

ACT III
The check appears. Three questions.

“Is this in your plan? Yes. Have you taken 2+ losses today? No. Friday after 15:30 — is this your swing or your boredom? Swing.”

The copilot draws three questions from state: plan match, loss count, time-of-week. Daniel answers. Each answer is logged against the trade record. The act of answering is what interrupts the autopilot. The questions take 24 seconds.

ACT IV
Verdict renders, cited.

“GREEN. Plan match, rule compliant, cortex 81, no active cooldown. Send.”

The copilot’s verdict is GREEN with a visible citation: plan.bias=long, rule.size_cap=OK, cortex=81>65, interlock=idle. Daniel clicks send. The broker adapter routes to FTMO. Fill at 1.2701. 15:34:02.

ACT V
The trade is never orphaned.

“Journal stub open. Mentor sees the entry in his dashboard. Luke gives it a thumb.”

At the moment of fill, events fan out. The journal opens an auto-stub with the plan citation pre-filled. The copilot records the setup signature for pattern detection. Luke — his mentor — sees the entry in the mentor dashboard (Daniel has opted in) and adds a single-tap thumb. The trade was witnessed by four systems before the candle closed.

F02 · VI · CONNECTED

The Cockpit terminates the other surfaces. Every service above runs before this click.

05 surfaces

Every other surface in Archio is upstream of the Cockpit. The Network carries the contract; System OS measures the body; Forecast returns the number; Copilot writes the verdict; Dashboard AI has the history. The Cockpit is the one surface that writes the event to the market, and for that reason it reads all five — and writes back to all five — on every click.

Surface Reads into the interlock Writes back from the ticket
F01 Networkcommunity layer Active mentor rules and the standing covenant. Any rule marked “hard” blocks the send outright; any rule marked “soft” triggers a three-second hold with citation. Every rule-override the trader signs in the hold window — relayed to the mentor’s feed as a signed consent event, never as a silent skip.
F03 System OSattention layer The live state flag at click-time. “Agitated” and “drifting” trigger the pre-send questions; “focused” lets the ticket through at normal latency. The full telemetry trace around the click — cadence, hover path, hesitation — fed back to System OS for state-model training.
F04 Forecastprobability layer Expected value in R for this exact setup, in this exact state. If EV falls below the trader’s signed threshold, the interlock highlights the gap inside the ticket. The actual outcome in R once the position closes — so Forecast can update the trader’s personal sample with real, not modelled, results.
F05 Copilotverdict layer The one-sentence verdict and its four citation chips. If Copilot says “hold,” the ticket shows the reason inline and offers a three-second re-think, not a cancel. The trader’s reason-for-proceed in his own words — which Copilot uses to update its confidence model on this specific setup family.
F06 Dashboard AImemory layer Similar-trade history, last 90 days. Shown inline on the ticket: “last 7 of this setup: +2R, –1R, –1R, +4R, –0.5R…” so the trader chooses with evidence. The full six-beat event — intent, interlock, hold, proceed, fill, close — signed and written to the append-only ledger.
F02 · VII · BUILT FOR

Four readers. One ticket. Four reasons to make it conscious.

04 readers

The order ticket is the one surface every trader meets, regardless of stage or style. The Cockpit was designed for four readers, each of whom brings a different form of risk to the click. The cards name each reader, their one-line need, and what the Cockpit gives them that MT5, cTrader, and TradingView never could.

W · 01 The Learner
“I click too fast. I always know it was wrong five minutes later.”

A wall he asked for, before the wall asks for him.

The learner does not need education — he needs a pause he cannot bypass in a tab. The Cockpit’s three-second hold is the first time the market has ever given him a polite reason to reconsider. Discipline, installed in the ticket, not the personality.

W · 02 The Grower
“My setups are fine. My size is where I lose money.”

Autosize, bound to the plan.

The grower has a sizing rule he breaks once a week. The Cockpit reads the rule from his plan, autosizes the ticket to comply, and forces him to sign any exception. The exception becomes a number; the number becomes a pattern; the pattern becomes a fix.

W · 03 The Leader
“My students copy my size. Some of them shouldn’t.”

Size by covenant, not by admiration.

When the leader posts a signed callout, the Cockpit in each follower’s account respects that follower’s risk profile — not the leader’s. One callout, many correctly-sized tickets. The leader’s generosity stops being his liability.

W · 04 The Mentor
“I want to know what they skipped, not what they did.”

Every override is a signed paragraph.

The Cockpit gives the mentor the exception log, not the fill log. Every hold the student bypassed, with his own words and the rule he overrode, lives in a reviewable feed. The Sunday call stops being a confession booth; it becomes a debrief.

F02 · COCKPIT
The first conscious order ticket in retail trading history.

Opinion. Autosize. Check. Verdict. Witness. Six frictionless realities answered with six conscious mechanics, running on one server-side interlock. The Cockpit is not a better MT5. It is the wall between intent and the market.

FEATURE · 06

Dashboard AI · The Archio Brain

/archio/brain · memory layer · append-only ledger

Every other feature in Archio is a room. Dashboard AI is the house. It is the brain that lives above, under, and beside every other surface. It is summoned in 180ms. It speaks the language of the trader, the mentor, the student, and the desk. It reads the screen he is looking at, answers the question he is asking, builds the view that does not yet exist, and logs every action it takes. It is not a chatbot. It is a console.

Archio Brain · Always listening · Never speaking first v0.6.2 · 180ms wake · 80ms reply

Press ⌘K. The Brain is the product.

The trader never asks where a feature is. He asks what he wants. The Brain reads six modules at once — Network, Forecast, System OS, Copilot, Forge, Journal — plus the screen he is currently looking at, and replies with an answer, a view, a navigation, or an action. It cites every claim. It logs every keystroke. It is the closest a retail trader will ever come to having a head of research, a compliance officer, an assistant, and a mentor answer a single question at the same time.

F06 · I · THE EIGHT POWERS

What the Brain can do that a chatbot cannot.

08 · 08

A chatbot takes a question and returns a paragraph. The Brain takes a question and returns an answer, a navigation, a view, a citation, an action, or all five at once. Below, the eight powers that make Dashboard AI a category of its own — each with the real capabilities nested inside it.

POWER · 01
Navigate
Teleport · by voice or text

Ask for any page, tab, filter, or deep-link by plain sentence. The Brain parses intent, resolves the route, and moves the trader there with state pre-applied. No menus. No clicks. No muscle memory.

  • DEEP-LINKopen Forge on NAS, London preset, 15m
  • SESSIONgo to my journal for trade #847
  • PERSONAtake me to Luke’s morning call
  • TIMEshow my stats for last Tuesday only
POWER · 02
See
Read the screen · always

The Brain sees what the trader sees. Pair, timeframe, indicators, journal notes, even the PDF he has open. Ask "what am I looking at" and get an answer framed in the context of the exact pixels on screen.

  • OCRreads every number, every level, every stamp
  • ZONESdetects S/R, trendlines, patterns
  • CAPTIONSreads comments, tweets, chat lines
  • DIFFcompares this view to last week’s
POWER · 03
Identify
Who is that · what is that

Point at anything — a face in a call, a handle on Twitter, a screenshot of a Discord message, a pattern on a chart — and ask "who is this" or "what is this." The Brain resolves to a record it can cite.

  • TRADERresolve @handles to verified profiles
  • QUOTEtrace a message back to its mentor
  • PATTERNname a setup using the trader’s taxonomy
  • INSTRUMENTidentify pair, session, correlation
POWER · 04
Build
Pages that don’t exist yet

The Brain builds bespoke views. Charts, tables, overlays, heatmaps, leaderboards, confusion matrices. A generative page-builder that takes a question and returns a surface. The surface is saveable, pinnable, shareable.

  • CHARTA over B with condition C, timeframe D
  • TABLEtrades grouped by tag, sorted by Sharpe
  • MATRIXmy setups × session × outcome
  • OVERLAYmentor entries on my chart
POWER · 05
Recall
Cited memory · never hallucinate

Every claim the Brain makes is tied to a record. A journal entry, a trade, a timestamp in a call, a chat line, a published note. The trader can click the citation and land on the source. If the Brain does not have a source, it says so.

  • TRADEScitations down to tick time
  • CALLSjump to exact second of mentor audio
  • NOTESevery line cross-linked to a trade
  • HONESTYwill return “I don’t have that”
POWER · 06
Act
Inside explicit rails

The Brain drafts, prepares, schedules, alerts, tags, exports. It prepares a ticket but does not send it. It drafts a note but does not post it. It queues an alert but does not fire it. The trader is always the last click.

  • PREPa ticket with rationale and risk
  • ALERTwhen DXY breaks 104 and Forge is open
  • DRAFTa post-trade journal entry, in the trader’s voice
  • EXPORTany view to CSV, PDF, share-link
POWER · 07
Teach
Explain, using his own data

The Brain explains concepts. Not generic ones — the trader’s own. Ask "what is a break-and-retest" and it answers using three of his breaks, two of which worked and one of which didn’t. Learning is never abstract.

  • CONCEPTexplained via the trader’s history
  • MISTAKEnamed, dated, quantified
  • EDGEdefined from his own hit-rate
  • DRILLassignable, review-ready
POWER · 08
Summon
On any page · in any state

⌘K on desktop. Long-press bottom-bar on mobile. Say "Brain" on the desk mic. Tap the sigil on any page. The Brain opens in 180ms with the current context pre-loaded. It never interrupts a trade in flight.

  • KEYBOARD⌘K / Ctrl-K · global
  • VOICEwake word “Brain” · push-to-talk
  • MOBILElong-press · haptic confirm
  • GUARDsilent during order staging

F06 · IV · THE VOICE

Say “Brain”, and it is in the room.

push-to-talk

The Brain has a voice interface because a trader on a desk cannot type while he is watching price. Wake word is a soft “Brain.” Push-to-talk is ⌘-space. Whisper is for private asks (the Brain replies only on his headphones). No always-listening pipe to the cloud — wake-word detection is local, on-device, and never records until the word fires.

Wake word · “Brain”
One word, 180 milliseconds, and the console is open.

The wake word runs in a sealed local model. No audio leaves the device until the trader says the word — and the model can be set to “no audio ever” for desks that prohibit it. Keyboard works on every machine; voice is a choice.

When he speaks, the Brain transcribes, routes, and replies. Every transcript is journaled, encrypted, exportable, and deletable. The trader owns the recording the same way he owns his chart.

Wakelocal Transcriptprivate Whisperheadphones Mutealways-available
Listening · on-device · encrypted
F06 · V · MODEL ROUTING

Under the hood — which model answers which ask.

06 lanes

The Brain is not one model. It is a router over six. Small, specialised, fast models handle the 95% of asks that do not need a frontier reasoner. A frontier model is invoked only for the 5% that do. This is how the Brain is both honest and cheap — and how it never sends your trading data to a model that did not need it.
